worked_examples.narrative: Forty-five thousand six hundred and seventeen divided by eleven is four thousand one hundred and forty-seven exactly, and rounding to zero decimals leaves it unchanged.

worked_examples.description: The same extraction of a balance that does not divide exactly
worked_examples.narrative: Forty-five thousand six hundred and twenty divided by eleven is four thousand one hundred and forty-seven point two seven two seven and so on, which rounds down to four thousand one hundred and forty-seven.

worked_examples.description: A balance eight higher
worked_examples.narrative: Forty-five thousand six hundred and twenty-eight divided by eleven is four thousand one hundred and forty-eight exactly.

records.name: Redirecting the reference resolution of an aggregation to another report
records.purpose: Lets one report read a figure of another report, which is how an annual summary pulls the boxes of the quarterly returns that feed it.

operands.name: the reference of the clause
operands.unit_or_currency: a numeric identifier, or an external identifier of the shape of a package name, a period and a name
operands.source: the clause of the subformula
operands.constraints: must resolve to a report and must not name the expression's own report

operands.name: the references of the formula
operands.source: the formula of the expression
operands.constraints: resolved inside the named report instead of the expression's own report

preconditions.condition: The formula matches the aggregation grammar from its first character to its last.
preconditions.otherwise: The write is refused with the message that reproduces the invalid formula for the named expression label of the named line, followed by the formula.

preconditions.condition: Every reference names a line code and an expression label that exist in the report, or in the report named by a cross-report clause.
preconditions.otherwise: The expression cannot be evaluated: the cell is rendered empty and the condition is reported to the designer.

preconditions.condition: The dependency graph of the referenced expressions has no cycle.
preconditions.otherwise: Evaluation stops and reports that the aggregation formulas of this report form a cycle through the named line code.

preconditions.condition: The clause is well formed, resolves to an existing report and does not name the expression's own report.
preconditions.otherwise: The three cross-report errors of the entities document are raised while the dependency graph is expanded.

procedure: Read the report reference inside the clause and resolve it to a report definition.
Restrict the resolution of every reference of the formula to the lines of that report.
Include the referenced expressions of that report in the collected expressions, so that they are evaluated before this one.
Evaluate the arithmetic over the figures obtained.
records.formula:
the references code.label of the formula are resolved inside the report named by the clause,
not inside the report the expression belongs to; the arithmetic is otherwise unchanged

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded by the redirection.
rounding.precision: Not applicable.
rounding.step: The redirection happens while the dependency graph is expanded, before any evaluation.

result.name: figure of the aggregation
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed in the cell of the line of the referring report.

edge_cases.case: The clause names the expression's own report.
edge_cases.outcome: It is refused: a cross-report clause may not be self-referential.

edge_cases.case: The named report does not exist.
edge_cases.outcome: The clause is unresolvable and the cross-report error is raised.

edge_cases.case: The named report is rendered with a different date option.
edge_cases.outcome: The reference is resolved for the same period column as the referring expression; the other report is evaluated with the referring report's options.

worked_examples.description: An annual summary line pulling one quarterly box
worked_examples.narrative: The reference is resolved inside the report whose external identifier is the one named by the clause, and the figure of two thousand four hundred and thirteen point five five is carried into the summary line.

records.name: Splitting an account code prefix formula into terms
records.purpose: Turns the text of an account code prefix formula into the signed terms the engine evaluates, including the subtlety that decides whether a trailing letter is a balance character or part of the code prefix.

operands.name: the formula text
operands.unit_or_currency: a text of prefixes, signs, exclusions and balance characters
operands.source: the expression of the report line
operands.constraints: must parse entirely; a term whose selector comes out empty is refused

operands.name: the exclusion lists
operands.unit_or_currency: prefixes of letters, digits and periods
operands.source: the parentheses that follow a selector
operands.constraints: may be empty, which is the escape mechanism for a code ending in a balance character

operands.name: the balance characters
operands.unit_or_currency: the letter that stands for a debit balance or the letter that stands for a credit balance
operands.source: the last character of a term
operands.constraints: recognised only when the selector does not end with one of those two letters, or when an exclusion follows

preconditions.condition: Every term matches the term grammar of an optional sign, a selector, an optional exclusion and an optional balance character.
preconditions.otherwise: The formula is refused with the formula error of the expression rules.

preconditions.condition: No term has an empty selector.
preconditions.otherwise: That term is refused with the formula error of the expression rules.

procedure: Remove every space from the formula.
Split the remaining text immediately before every plus sign and every minus sign, and discard a leading empty piece produced when the formula starts with a sign.

For each piece, read the optional leading sign, then the selector, which is either a run of letters, digits and periods or the tag selector naming a tag by its numeric identifier or its external identifier.
Read an exclusion when a parenthesised list follows the selector, and read a balance character when one of the two letters closes the term.

Apply the parsing subtlety: the selector may not end with either balance character letter unless an exclusion immediately follows it, so a term of two digits followed by the debit letter parses as that two-digit selector with a debit balance character, while the same text followed by an empty exclusion parses as a three-character selector with no balance character.
records.formula:
terms = split( remove_spaces( formula ) , before every + and every − )
term  = [ sign ] selector [ exclusion ] [ balance_character ]

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded: the parsing produces terms, not amounts.
rounding.precision: Not applicable.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: the ordered list of signed terms
result.stored_or_displayed: Not displayed; each term is evaluated and the signed contributions are added into the figure of the expression.

edge_cases.case: A term's selector comes out empty.
edge_cases.outcome: The term is refused with the formula error of the expression rules.

edge_cases.case: An account code genuinely ends with a balance character letter.
edge_cases.outcome: An empty exclusion is written after it, which forces the letter into the selector and leaves the term without a balance character.

edge_cases.case: The formula begins with a sign.
edge_cases.outcome: The leading empty piece produced by the split is discarded and the first real term carries that sign.

edge_cases.case: A term carries no sign.
edge_cases.outcome: It is treated as positive, including the first term.

worked_examples.description: A formula of three terms with exclusions
worked_examples.narrative: Spaces are removed and the text is split before each sign, giving the unsigned first term and two signed terms, each carrying its own exclusion list.

worked_examples.description: A code that ends with the debit balance letter
worked_examples.narrative: The empty exclusion forces the selector to be the three characters, so the term matches accounts whose code starts with those three characters, whatever the sign of their balance.

worked_examples.description: The same three characters without an exclusion
worked_examples.narrative: Without an exclusion the trailing letter is read as the debit balance character and the selector is the two digits.

records.name: Selecting the accounts of a term
records.purpose: Determines which accounts one term of an account code prefix formula reads, by code prefix or by account tag, less the accounts its exclusion removes.

operands.name: the selector
operands.unit_or_currency: a code prefix, or a tag named by its numeric identifier or its external identifier
operands.source: the term
operands.constraints: compared as text and case-sensitively

operands.name: the excluded prefixes
operands.unit_or_currency: prefixes of letters, digits and periods
operands.source: the exclusion of the term
operands.constraints: each removes every account whose code starts with it

operands.name: the account codes of the selected companies
operands.unit_or_currency: codes as seen by the selected company
operands.source: the chart of accounts
operands.constraints: a company-dependent code is read as the selected company sees it

preconditions.condition: The tag named by a tag selector exists.
preconditions.otherwise: The term selects no account and contributes zero.

preconditions.condition: At least one company is selected.
preconditions.otherwise: There is no chart of accounts to read and the term contributes zero.

procedure: For a code prefix selector, take every account of the selected companies whose code, compared as text, starts with that prefix.
For a tag selector, take every account of the selected companies carrying the account tag named by the numeric identifier or the external identifier inside the parentheses.
Remove from that set every account whose code starts with any of the excluded prefixes, whether the selector was a code prefix or a tag.
Keep the resulting set as the accounts of the term.
records.formula:
accounts( term ) = { accounts of the selected companies matching the selector }
                 − { accounts whose code starts with one of the excluded prefixes }

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded: the term selects accounts, not amounts.
rounding.precision: Not applicable.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: the accounts of the term
result.stored_or_displayed: Not displayed; the balances of these accounts are summed into the term value, and the drill-down presents them as the term's own group.

edge_cases.case: An account's code is company-dependent.
edge_cases.outcome: The prefix comparison uses the code as seen by the selected company, so an account coded with six digits in one company and eight in another matches a three-digit prefix in both.

edge_cases.case: Two companies use the same code for different accounts.
edge_cases.outcome: A consolidated report merges them into one line by code; giving one of them a distinct code through the account code mapping is the remedy when that is wrong.

edge_cases.case: An account is selected by two terms of the same formula.
edge_cases.outcome: It contributes to both: the engine does not deduplicate across terms, which is why exclusions exist.

edge_cases.case: The comparison is a prefix comparison, not an equality.
edge_cases.outcome: A code of eight digits matches a four-digit term when its first four digits are that term.

edge_cases.case: An account is archived.
edge_cases.outcome: Its items are still read.

worked_examples.description: A term over a code prefix with two exclusions

expected_outputs.accounts_selected: every account of the selected companies whose code starts with the two digits, less those whose code starts with either three-digit prefix

worked_examples.narrative: The prefix selects the whole family and the two exclusions remove the two sub-families, leaving the rest of the family.

worked_examples.description: A formula of three tag and prefix terms

expected_outputs.term_1_accounts: the accounts carrying the tag identified by the external identifier
expected_outputs.term_2_accounts: the accounts carrying the tag whose numeric identifier is 42
expected_outputs.term_3_accounts: the accounts whose code starts with the two digits

worked_examples.narrative: A tag may be named by an external identifier or by a numeric identifier, and tag terms and code prefix terms may be mixed in one formula.

worked_examples.description: A term over a tag with a balance character and a term over a tag with an exclusion

expected_outputs.accounts_selected_1: the tagged accounts whose balance is a credit
expected_outputs.accounts_selected_2: the tagged accounts whose code does not start with the two digits

worked_examples.narrative: Exclusions and balance characters apply to a tag selector exactly as they apply to a code prefix selector.

records.name: The value of a term without a balance character
records.purpose: Gives the figure one term of an account code prefix formula contributes when every account it selects is counted, whatever the direction of that account's balance.

operands.name: the accounts of the term
operands.source: the selection rules of the term
operands.constraints: may be empty

operands.name: the matching Journal Items
operands.unit_or_currency: items carrying amounts in the presentation currency
operands.source: the ledger, restricted by the base restriction, by the date window of the expression's date scope and by the condition that the item's account is one of the term's accounts
operands.constraints: each item is counted once

operands.name: debit and credit of each item
operands.source: the Journal Item
operands.constraints: not negative

preconditions.condition: The term parsed and its selector is not empty.
preconditions.otherwise: The formula is refused with the formula error of the expression rules.

procedure: Select the accounts of the term.
Take the Journal Items that satisfy the base restriction, that fall in the date window of the expression's date scope, and whose account is one of the term's accounts.
Add the debit and subtract the credit of every such item, accumulating at full stored precision.
records.formula: term_value = Σ over items m on the accounts of the term of ( debit(m) − credit(m) )

rounding.precision: The decimal places of the presentation currency, and then the whole unit when the report sets an integer rounding mode.
rounding.step: Only at display; the term value is accumulated at full stored precision.

result.name: term value
result.stored_or_displayed: Not displayed on its own: it is multiplied by the term's sign and added into the figure of the expression.

edge_cases.case: The term selects no account.
edge_cases.outcome: The term value is zero.

edge_cases.case: The term selects accounts with balances of both directions.
edge_cases.outcome: They are netted, because no balance character is applied.

edge_cases.case: The date window is unbounded below and the accounts do not carry forward.
edge_cases.outcome: The carry-forward correction limits each such account to its own fiscal year.

worked_examples.description: A term over a two-digit prefix matching two accounts
worked_examples.narrative: Minus forty-two plus twenty-five is minus seventeen, the netted total of the family.

worked_examples.description: A term summing a family whose codes are longer than the prefix
worked_examples.narrative: The comparison is a prefix comparison, so an eight-digit code matches a four-digit term and its balance of one thousand one hundred and eighty point two five enters the term.

records.name: The balance of a single account inside a term
records.purpose: Gives the figure that decides, account by account, whether an account passes the balance character filter, which is the only place in the domain where a per-account total is needed.

operands.name: the account
operands.unit_or_currency: one account of the term's set
operands.source: the selection rules of the term
operands.constraints: tested individually

operands.name: the matching Journal Items of that account
operands.unit_or_currency: items carrying amounts in the presentation currency
operands.source: the ledger, restricted by the base restriction and by the date window of the expression's date scope
operands.constraints: only the items of that one account

operands.name: debit and credit of each item
operands.source: the Journal Item
operands.constraints: not negative

preconditions.condition: The term carries a balance character.
preconditions.otherwise: No per-account balance is needed and the term is evaluated as a single sum over all of its accounts.

procedure: Take the Journal Items of that one account that satisfy the base restriction and fall in the date window.
Add the debit and subtract the credit of every such item.
Use the result only to decide whether the account is kept by the balance character.
records.formula: account_balance(a) = Σ over items m on account a of ( debit(m) − credit(m) )

rounding.precision: Full stored precision while the sign is tested; the presentation precision only once the kept balances have been summed.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, at display.
rounding.step: No rounding before the sign test, so that a balance of a fraction of a unit is not turned into zero by rounding.

result.name: balance of one account over the window
result.stored_or_displayed: Not displayed; it decides whether the account contributes and, when it does, it is the amount it contributes.

edge_cases.case: The account has no item in the window.
edge_cases.outcome: Its balance is zero and it is kept by neither balance character.

edge_cases.case: The filter is per account.
edge_cases.outcome: It is not per item and not per term total, which is what lets one line show only the customers in debit and another only those in credit.

edge_cases.case: The account carries forward and the window is unbounded below.
edge_cases.outcome: Its balance accumulates all history; an account that does not carry forward starts at the beginning of the fiscal year that contains the window's upper bound.

worked_examples.description: Two accounts of the same family over the same window
worked_examples.narrative: The first account totals a credit of forty-two, so its balance is minus forty-two; the second totals a debit of twenty-five, so its balance is twenty-five.

records.name: The value of a term with the debit balance character
records.purpose: Keeps only the accounts of a term whose own balance is a debit, which is how a report shows, on one line, only the counterparties that owe the company.

operands.name: the accounts of the term
operands.source: the selection rules of the term
operands.constraints: each is tested individually

operands.name: the balance of each account over the window
operands.source: the per-account balance of the term
operands.constraints: an account whose balance is exactly zero is kept by neither balance character

preconditions.condition: The term ends with the debit balance character and the selector does not itself end with it, or an exclusion separates them.
preconditions.otherwise: The letter is part of the selector and no filter is applied.

procedure: Select the accounts of the term.
Compute the balance of each account over the base restriction and the date window.
Keep an account when its balance is strictly greater than zero.
Add the balances of the kept accounts.
records.formula: term_value = Σ over the accounts a of the term with account_balance(a) > 0 of account_balance(a)

rounding.what: The sum of the kept balances.
rounding.precision: The decimal places of the presentation currency, and then the whole unit when the report sets an integer rounding mode.
rounding.step: Only at display; the per-account balances are compared and summed at full stored precision.

result.name: term value
result.stored_or_displayed: Not displayed on its own: it is multiplied by the term's sign and added into the figure of the expression; the drill-down lists only the kept accounts.

edge_cases.case: An account's balance is exactly zero.
edge_cases.outcome: It is excluded, because the test is strictly greater than zero.

edge_cases.case: Every account of the term has a credit balance.
edge_cases.outcome: The term value is zero.

edge_cases.case: The same term is written without the balance character.
edge_cases.outcome: The credit balances would net against the debit balances, which is a different figure.

worked_examples.description: A term over a two-digit prefix, filtered to debit balances
worked_examples.narrative: The first account has a credit balance and is dropped; the second has a debit balance of twenty-five and is kept, so the term contributes twenty-five instead of the netted minus seventeen.

records.name: The value of a term with the credit balance character
records.purpose: Keeps only the accounts of a term whose own balance is a credit, which is the mirror line of the debit filter and shows the counterparties the company owes.

operands.name: the accounts of the term
operands.source: the selection rules of the term
operands.constraints: each is tested individually

operands.name: the balance of each account over the window
operands.source: the per-account balance of the term
operands.constraints: an account whose balance is exactly zero is kept by neither balance character

preconditions.condition: The term ends with the credit balance character and the selector does not itself end with it, or an exclusion separates them.
preconditions.otherwise: The letter is part of the selector and no filter is applied.

procedure: Select the accounts of the term.
Compute the balance of each account over the base restriction and the date window.
Keep an account when its balance is strictly lower than zero.
Add the balances of the kept accounts, which gives a negative figure or zero.
records.formula: term_value = Σ over the accounts a of the term with account_balance(a) < 0 of account_balance(a)

rounding.what: The sum of the kept balances.
rounding.precision: The decimal places of the presentation currency, and then the whole unit when the report sets an integer rounding mode.
rounding.step: Only at display; the per-account balances are compared and summed at full stored precision.

result.name: term value
result.stored_or_displayed: Not displayed on its own: it is multiplied by the term's sign and added into the figure of the expression; a leading minus on the term turns it into a positive amount owed.

edge_cases.case: An account's balance is exactly zero.
edge_cases.outcome: It is excluded, because the test is strictly lower than zero.

edge_cases.case: The term is written with a leading minus.
edge_cases.outcome: The negative sum becomes positive, which is how a liability line shows an amount owed as a positive figure.

edge_cases.case: A tag selector carries the credit balance character.
edge_cases.outcome: Only the tagged accounts whose balance is a credit are kept.

worked_examples.description: A term over a two-digit prefix, filtered to credit balances
worked_examples.narrative: The second account has a debit balance and is dropped; the first has a credit balance of minus forty-two and is kept, so the term contributes minus forty-two.

records.name: Combining the terms of an account code prefix formula
records.purpose: Adds the signed contributions of the terms into the single figure of the expression, which is the last step of the engine most statements are built on.

operands.name: the term values
operands.source: the evaluation of each term, with or without a balance character
operands.constraints: one value per term

operands.name: the sign of each term
operands.source: the leading sign of the term
operands.constraints: minus one when the term carried a leading minus, plus one otherwise, including for a first term with no sign

preconditions.condition: Every term parsed and every selector is non-empty.
preconditions.otherwise: The formula is refused with the formula error of the expression rules.

procedure: Evaluate every term of the formula, applying its exclusion and its balance character.
Multiply each term value by minus one when the term carried a leading minus, and by plus one otherwise.
Add the signed contributions.
Do not deduplicate accounts across terms: an account selected by two terms contributes to both.
records.formula:
formula_value = Σ over the terms t of ( sign(t) × term_value(t) )
                where sign(t) = −1 for a term with a leading minus and +1 otherwise

rounding.precision: The decimal places of the presentation currency, and then the whole unit when the report sets an integer rounding mode.
rounding.step: Only at display; the term values are added at full stored precision.

result.name: figure of the expression
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed in the cell of the line and of the column bound to the expression's label; the drill-down presents each contributing term as its own group so that the signs remain visible.

edge_cases.case: A formula writes a family and one of its sub-families as two positive terms.
edge_cases.outcome: The sub-family is counted twice, which is why exclusions exist.

edge_cases.case: A formula mixes terms with and without a balance character, for example a debit-filtered family, a credit-filtered family with an exclusion and an unfiltered family.
edge_cases.outcome: Each term applies its own filter before it contributes, and the signs are then applied term by term; the filters never interact across terms.

edge_cases.case: A formula is a single negated prefix.
edge_cases.outcome: The family's credit total is displayed as a positive amount, which is what several national definitions do.

edge_cases.case: A term with a balance character contributes.
edge_cases.outcome: Only the accounts it kept appear in the drill-down of that term.

worked_examples.description: A formula of three terms with exclusions
worked_examples.narrative: Minus seventeen plus three thousand four hundred and eighty minus one thousand two hundred is two thousand two hundred and sixty-three.

worked_examples.description: A shipped single negated prefix
worked_examples.narrative: The family totals a credit of four thousand three hundred and ten and the leading minus turns it into a positive four thousand three hundred and ten.

worked_examples.description: A shipped sum of five prefixes
worked_examples.narrative: Nine hundred plus one hundred and twenty point five zero plus zero plus forty-five plus twelve point seven five is one thousand and seventy-eight point two five.

records.name: The sum of the external values of an expression
records.purpose: Brings figures that are not in the ledger into a report: the amounts a filer typed by hand and the amounts an earlier period carried forward, added over the window of the expression's date scope.

operands.name: the external values targeting the expression
operands.source: the stored external values whose target expression is this expression and whose company is one of the selected companies
operands.constraints: only those whose date falls in the date window of the expression's date scope

operands.name: the value of each record
operands.source: the external value record
operands.constraints: a textual value is used instead when the display type is text, in which case only the most recent value is meaningful

preconditions.condition: The formula is one of the two accepted words, the one that sums and the one that takes the most recent value.
preconditions.otherwise: The expression produces no figure; five shipped expressions carry other text and are defects in the shipped data, not an extension of the grammar.

preconditions.condition: The external values carry the company of the reading, which is required on the record.
preconditions.otherwise: The record is refused by the validation that makes an external value company-scoped and required.

procedure: Take the external values whose target expression is this expression.
Keep those whose company is one of the selected companies.
Keep those whose date falls inside the date window of the expression's date scope.
Add their values.
Apply the rounding clause of the subformula when one is present, and the decimal places of the presentation currency otherwise.
records.formula: result = Σ over the external values v in the window of value(v)

rounding.what: The sum of the selected values.
rounding.precision: The number of decimals named by the rounding clause of the subformula, and the decimal places of the presentation currency when there is none.
rounding.step: After the selection, before display and before the value is stored when the user types one.

result.name: figure of the expression
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed in the cell; the drill-down lists the external value records behind it with their date, their name, their company and their amount, rather than Journal Items.

edge_cases.case: No external value falls in the window.
edge_cases.outcome: The figure is zero, not empty.

edge_cases.case: A record falls outside the window.
edge_cases.outcome: It is excluded, even when it targets the same expression.

edge_cases.case: The display type of the expression or of the column is text.
edge_cases.outcome: The textual value is used and the sum is not meaningful; only the most recent value is used with textual values.

edge_cases.case: A saved journal-item filter is active.
edge_cases.outcome: It is never applied to this engine, which reads no Journal Item.

worked_examples.description: An adjustment line of a quarterly return with three records, one of them outside the window
worked_examples.narrative: The record of the ninth of July falls outside the quarter, so two hundred and forty plus minus zero point three five gives two hundred and thirty-nine point six five.

records.name: The most recent external value of an expression
records.purpose: Reads one single figure rather than a total, which is what the carry-over mechanism needs so that re-closing a period never adds a second copy of the same amount.

operands.name: the external values targeting the expression
operands.unit_or_currency: the presentation currency, or a text, or a yes or no value
operands.source: the stored external values whose target expression is this expression and whose company is one of the selected companies
operands.constraints: only those whose date falls in the date window of the expression's date scope

operands.name: the ordering
operands.unit_or_currency: date ascending, then stored identifier ascending
operands.source: the records themselves
operands.constraints: the last record of that ordering is the one read

preconditions.condition: The formula is one of the two accepted words, the one that sums and the one that takes the most recent value.
preconditions.otherwise: The expression produces no figure; five shipped expressions carry other text and are defects in the shipped data, not an extension of the grammar.

preconditions.condition: The external values carry the company of the reading, which is required on the record.
preconditions.otherwise: The record is refused by the validation that makes an external value company-scoped and required.

procedure: Take the external values whose target expression is this expression, whose company is one of the selected companies, and whose date falls in the date window of the expression's date scope.
Order them by date ascending and then by stored identifier ascending.
Take the value of the last record of that ordering.
Return zero when no record was selected.
records.formula:
result = value of the last record, ordered by date then by identifier, of the external values in the window
result = 0    when no such record exists

rounding.precision: The number of decimals named by the rounding clause of the subformula, and the decimal places of the presentation currency when there is none.
rounding.step: After the selection, at display.

result.name: figure of the expression
result.unit_or_currency: the presentation currency, a text, or a rendered tick or cross
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed in the cell; the drill-down lists the external value records rather than Journal Items.

edge_cases.case: Two records share a date.
edge_cases.outcome: The one with the greater stored identifier wins, because the ordering falls back on the identifier.

edge_cases.case: No record falls in the window.
edge_cases.outcome: The figure is zero.

edge_cases.case: The display type is text.
edge_cases.outcome: The textual value of the selected record is displayed.

edge_cases.case: The display type is a yes or no value.
edge_cases.outcome: The cell renders a tick or a cross and carries no amount at all, which is how three flags of the Italian monthly return are typed by the filer.

edge_cases.case: A second record was written for the same period.
edge_cases.outcome: The most recent one wins rather than both being added, which is why the carry-over mechanism uses this formula and not the sum.

worked_examples.description: The same three adjustment records read with the most recent value instead of the sum
worked_examples.narrative: The record of the second of May is the last one inside the quarter, so its value of minus zero point three five is the figure.

records.name: The rounding clause of an external value expression
records.purpose: Fixes the number of decimals an external figure is rounded to, both for display and for the amount stored when a user types one, so that a declaration of whole amounts never stores fractions.

operands.name: the figure
operands.source: the sum or the most recent value of the external values, or the amount the user typed
operands.constraints: any value

operands.name: the number of decimal places
operands.source: the digits after the rounding clause of the subformula
operands.constraints: zero means whole numbers

preconditions.condition: The subformula carries the rounding clause.
preconditions.otherwise: The figure is rounded to the decimal places of the presentation currency instead.

procedure: Obtain the figure, either by the sum or by the most recent value, or from the cell the user typed into.
Read the number of decimal places from the rounding clause.
Round the figure to that many decimal places, carrying a half away from zero.
Use the rounded figure both for display and for the value stored when the user typed one.
records.formula:
rounded_value = sign( value ) × floor( | value | × 10ⁿ + 0.5 ) ÷ 10ⁿ
                where n is the number of decimal places of the rounding clause

rounding.precision: The number of decimal places of the clause; the two most frequent shipped subformulas make the cell editable with two decimals, on four hundred and sixty-five expressions, and editable with whole numbers, on two hundred and eight expressions.
rounding.step: After the sum or the selection, and before the value is stored when the user types one.

result.name: rounded external figure
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed in the cell and stored on the external value record when the user typed the figure.

edge_cases.case: The clause names zero decimals.
edge_cases.outcome: The figure is a whole number, both on screen and in storage.

edge_cases.case: The subformula carries no rounding clause.
edge_cases.outcome: The decimal places of the presentation currency are used.

edge_cases.case: A bound clause is also present.
edge_cases.outcome: It behaves exactly as it does on an aggregation expression and is applied after the sum or the selection.

worked_examples.description: A typed adjustment of two hundred and forty point four nine five with two decimals
worked_examples.narrative: Two hundred and forty point four nine five rounded to two decimals carries the half away from zero and gives two hundred and forty point five zero, which is both displayed and stored.

worked_examples.description: The same figure on a box declared in whole amounts
worked_examples.narrative: Rounding to zero decimals gives two hundred and forty.

records.name: Creating or updating a manual external value
records.purpose: Records the figure a user types into an editable cell, so that a legal declaration can carry an amount the ledger does not contain, without producing any accounting entry.

operands.name: the typed figure
operands.source: the cell the user typed into
operands.constraints: rounded by the rounding clause of the subformula when there is one

operands.name: the target expression
operands.unit_or_currency: an expression of a report line
operands.source: the cell's line and the column's expression label
operands.constraints: must carry the clause that makes the cell editable

operands.name: the date
operands.source: the to-date currently selected in the report
operands.constraints: must not fall on or before an applicable lock date

operands.name: the active company
operands.source: the user's active company
operands.constraints: required on the record

preconditions.condition: The subformula of the expression carries the clause that makes the cell editable.
preconditions.otherwise: The write is refused: a manual figure requires an editable subformula.

preconditions.condition: The user holds the accounting manager group.
preconditions.otherwise: The write is refused: a manual figure requires that group.

preconditions.condition: The date does not fall on or before an applicable lock date.
preconditions.otherwise: The write is refused by the locking rules.

preconditions.condition: The company is set on the record.
preconditions.otherwise: The record is refused: an external value is company-scoped and required.

procedure: Determine the target expression from the cell's line and the column's expression label, and the date from the to-date currently selected in the report.
Search for an existing external value with that target expression, that date and the active company, whose origin line is empty, that is a manual value.
When one is found, write the typed figure into it, rounded by the rounding clause when the subformula carries one.
When none is found, create one with the target expression, the date, the active company, the rounded figure, a name derived from the line's name, and an empty origin line and origin expression label.
records.formula:
stored_value = round( typed_figure , decimals of the rounding clause )
the record is identified by ( target expression , date , company , empty origin line )

rounding.precision: The number of decimals of the rounding clause of the subformula, and the decimal places of the presentation currency when there is none.
rounding.step: Before the value is written, so that what is stored is exactly what is displayed.

result.name: manual external value
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored as an external value record and displayed in the cell; no Journal Entry is produced and no account balance changes.

edge_cases.case: A manual value already exists for the same target, date and company.
edge_cases.outcome: It is overwritten rather than duplicated, because a manual value is identified by its empty origin line.

edge_cases.case: A carry-over value exists for the same target and date.
edge_cases.outcome: It is a different record, because its origin line is set; the manual write never touches it.

edge_cases.case: The date falls in a locked period.
edge_cases.outcome: The write is refused by the locking rules; the lock date rules of the domain state the exact refusal.

edge_cases.case: The report has been adjusted by hand.
edge_cases.outcome: Its boxes will not tie to the ledger, which is intended: the closing entry always follows the ledger, never the declared boxes.

worked_examples.description: A filer typing a correction into an editable adjustment cell of a quarterly return
worked_examples.narrative: No manual record exists for that target, date and company, so one is created carrying two hundred and forty on the thirtieth of June, and no accounting entry is produced.

worked_examples.description: The same filer correcting the figure to two hundred and thirty
worked_examples.narrative: The existing manual record is found by its target, date, company and empty origin line, and its value is overwritten with two hundred and thirty.

records.name: The figure returned by a custom function
records.purpose: Provides figures no declarative formula can express, such as progressive brackets, multi-tier thresholds, loops over sub-periods, or amounts assembled from records outside the ledger.

operands.name: the expressions naming the function
operands.source: every expression of the report whose formula is this function's name
operands.constraints: all are passed in one call so that one call serves them all

operands.name: the resolved options
operands.unit_or_currency: the whole option set of the rendering, with the date window already computed per date scope
operands.source: the pipeline
operands.constraints: identical to what every other engine sees

operands.name: the base restriction
operands.source: the pipeline
operands.constraints: so that the function reads the same ledger slice as the other engines

operands.name: the current period index
operands.source: the pipeline
operands.constraints: says which comparison column is being computed

operands.name: the subformula of each expression
operands.unit_or_currency: a key of the mapping the function returns
operands.source: the expression
operands.constraints: a missing key yields no figure

preconditions.condition: The function is registered by an extension package under the name the formula gives.
preconditions.otherwise: The expression produces no figure and the cell is rendered empty.

preconditions.condition: The function is pure with respect to the ledger: the same options and the same ledger give the same figures, and it writes no record.
preconditions.otherwise: The report is not reproducible and a rendering could change the data it reads.

procedure: Collect every expression of the report whose formula names this function.
Call the function once with those expressions, the resolved options including the date window per date scope, the base restriction and the current period index.
Receive, for each expression, a mapping from key to figure.
Take the entry whose key equals that expression's subformula, and render the cell empty when the key is missing.
Treat the figure as not auditable unless the designer set the auditable flag by hand, in which case the function must also return a drill-down restriction.
records.formula:
figure( expression ) = the entry of the returned mapping whose key equals the expression's subformula
figure( expression ) = no figure, and the cell is rendered empty, when that key is absent

rounding.precision: The display type of the expression governs the rendering; a percentage display renders one decimal place.
rounding.method: Half away from zero at display, unless the function has already rounded.
rounding.step: The function rounds internally where its own rule requires it; the report rounds at display.

result.name: figure of the expression
result.unit_or_currency: the presentation currency, a plain number, or a percentage
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed in the cell; not auditable by default, because the engine cannot declare which Journal Items produced the figure.

edge_cases.case: The returned mapping has no entry for the expression's subformula.
edge_cases.outcome: No figure is produced and the cell is rendered empty.

edge_cases.case: The designer sets the auditable flag by hand.
edge_cases.outcome: The function must also return a drill-down restriction, or the audit action has nothing to show.

edge_cases.case: The function writes a record.
edge_cases.outcome: The contract is broken: a custom function must be pure with respect to the ledger.

edge_cases.case: Only twelve shipped expressions use this engine.
edge_cases.outcome: A rebuild that implements the other five engines exactly renders every shipped definition correctly except those twelve expressions.

worked_examples.description: The twelve expressions of the Bolivian report that read a proportion of the annual allowance consumed in a quarter
worked_examples.narrative: The function computes, for the quarter containing the report's to-date, the proportion of the annual allowance already consumed and returns it under the key the subformula names; the percentage display type renders the returned twenty-five as twenty-five point zero percent.

records.name: The window of the strict range date scope
records.purpose: Restricts an expression to the movement of the requested period and nothing else, which is what every line of a profit and loss statement and almost every box of a tax return needs.

operands.name: the from-date of the requested period
operands.source: the date option of the rendering
operands.constraints: equal to the to-date for a single-date report

operands.name: the to-date of the requested period
operands.source: the date option of the rendering
operands.constraints: not before the from-date

operands.name: the fiscal year containing the to-date
operands.unit_or_currency: a first day and a last day
operands.source: the company's fiscal-year-end day and month, and the declared fiscal year records where they exist
operands.constraints: for a company closing on the thirty-first of December, the fiscal year containing a date in 2026 runs from the first of January 2026 to the thirty-first of December 2026

preconditions.condition: The from-date is not after the to-date.
preconditions.otherwise: The period is empty and every ledger figure is zero; a rebuild should refuse the option rather than render zeros.

preconditions.condition: The fiscal-year boundaries of the company are known.
preconditions.otherwise: The default rule of the last day and month applies, and a fiscal year shorter or longer than twelve months is taken from the declared fiscal year records.

procedure: Take the from-date of the requested period as the lower bound.
Take the to-date of the requested period as the upper bound.
Include both bounds.
Apply no carry-forward correction: the window is the same for an account that carries forward and for one that does not.
records.formula:
lower_bound = date_from
upper_bound = date_to

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded: the result is a pair of dates.
rounding.precision: Whole days.
rounding.step: No rounding step; both bounds are inclusive as written.

result.name: the window of the expression
result.unit_or_currency: a first day and a last day, both inclusive
result.stored_or_displayed: Not displayed; it is conjoined with the base restriction by every ledger-reading engine, and it also selects the external values of an external expression.

edge_cases.case: The report is a single-date report.
edge_cases.outcome: The from-date equals the to-date and the window is that one day.

edge_cases.case: The account does not carry forward.
edge_cases.outcome: The window is unchanged, because the correction applies only to the three unbounded scopes.

edge_cases.case: The from-date is after the to-date.
edge_cases.outcome: The window is empty and every figure is zero.

worked_examples.description: The second quarter of a calendar fiscal year
worked_examples.narrative: The window is the requested period itself, for an asset account and for an income account alike.

records.name: The window of the from-beginning date scope
records.purpose: Accumulates every movement up to the report date, corrected per account, which is the single scope that lets one balance sheet line and one profit and loss line share a definition.

operands.name: the from-date of the requested period
operands.source: the date option of the rendering
operands.constraints: equal to the to-date for a single-date report

operands.name: the to-date of the requested period
operands.source: the date option of the rendering
operands.constraints: not before the from-date

operands.name: the fiscal year containing the to-date
operands.unit_or_currency: a first day and a last day
operands.source: the company's fiscal-year-end day and month, and the declared fiscal year records where they exist
operands.constraints: for a company closing on the thirty-first of December, the fiscal year containing a date in 2026 runs from the first of January 2026 to the thirty-first of December 2026

operands.name: whether the account carries forward
operands.source: the account: true when its internal group is neither income nor expense and its type is not current-year earnings
operands.constraints: evaluated per account, not per expression

preconditions.condition: The from-date is not after the to-date.
preconditions.otherwise: The period is empty and every ledger figure is zero; a rebuild should refuse the option rather than render zeros.

preconditions.condition: The fiscal-year boundaries of the company are known.
preconditions.otherwise: The default rule of the last day and month applies, and a fiscal year shorter or longer than twelve months is taken from the declared fiscal year records.

procedure: Take the to-date of the requested period as the upper bound.
Leave the lower bound open for an account that carries forward, so that the whole history is accumulated.
For an account that does not carry forward, set the lower bound to the first day of the fiscal year containing the upper bound.
Apply the correction per account, not once per expression, because one engine may read several accounts at once.
records.formula:
upper_bound = date_to
lower_bound = none                                             when the account carries forward
lower_bound = start of the fiscal year containing date_to      when the account does not carry forward

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded: the result is a pair of dates.
rounding.precision: Whole days.
rounding.step: No rounding step; both bounds are inclusive as written.

result.name: the window of the expression, per account
result.unit_or_currency: a first day, possibly open, and a last day, inclusive
result.stored_or_displayed: Not displayed; it is conjoined with the base restriction by every ledger-reading engine.

edge_cases.case: An asset or liability account.
edge_cases.outcome: It carries forward, so the window accumulates since the first entry ever posted.

edge_cases.case: An income or expense account.
edge_cases.outcome: It does not carry forward, so the window accumulates only within the fiscal year containing the report date.

edge_cases.case: The current-year earnings account.
edge_cases.outcome: Its type excludes it from carrying forward, so its line shows the result of the current fiscal year only.

edge_cases.case: An engine reads several accounts at once.
edge_cases.outcome: The correction is applied account by account inside the same evaluation.

worked_examples.description: A balance sheet line and a profit and loss line, both with this scope, over the second quarter of a calendar fiscal year
worked_examples.narrative: The asset account carries forward and accumulates all history up to the thirtieth of June; the income account does not and starts at the first of January.

records.name: The window of the from-fiscal-year date scope
records.purpose: Accumulates the movement of the current fiscal year up to the report date, whatever the account, which is what a year-to-date line needs.

operands.name: the from-date of the requested period
operands.source: the date option of the rendering
operands.constraints: equal to the to-date for a single-date report

operands.name: the to-date of the requested period
operands.source: the date option of the rendering
operands.constraints: not before the from-date

operands.name: the fiscal year containing the to-date
operands.unit_or_currency: a first day and a last day
operands.source: the company's fiscal-year-end day and month, and the declared fiscal year records where they exist
operands.constraints: for a company closing on the thirty-first of December, the fiscal year containing a date in 2026 runs from the first of January 2026 to the thirty-first of December 2026

preconditions.condition: The from-date is not after the to-date.
preconditions.otherwise: The period is empty and every ledger figure is zero; a rebuild should refuse the option rather than render zeros.

preconditions.condition: The fiscal-year boundaries of the company are known.
preconditions.otherwise: The default rule of the last day and month applies, and a fiscal year shorter or longer than twelve months is taken from the declared fiscal year records.

procedure: Take the first day of the fiscal year containing the to-date as the lower bound.
Take the to-date of the requested period as the upper bound.
Include both bounds.
Apply no carry-forward correction: the lower bound is already the start of the fiscal year.
records.formula:
lower_bound = fiscal_year_start
upper_bound = date_to

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded: the result is a pair of dates.
rounding.precision: Whole days.
rounding.step: No rounding step; both bounds are inclusive as written.

result.name: the window of the expression
result.unit_or_currency: a first day and a last day, both inclusive
result.stored_or_displayed: Not displayed; it is conjoined with the base restriction by every ledger-reading engine.

edge_cases.case: An account that carries forward.
edge_cases.outcome: Only its movement inside the fiscal year is read, which is how the allocated earnings of the current year are isolated on the balance sheet.

edge_cases.case: A fiscal year shorter or longer than twelve months.
edge_cases.outcome: The declared fiscal year records supply the boundaries.

edge_cases.case: The report date is the first day of the fiscal year.
edge_cases.outcome: The window is that one day.

worked_examples.description: A line with this scope over the second quarter of a calendar fiscal year
worked_examples.narrative: The window runs from the first of January to the thirtieth of June for an asset account and for an income account alike.

records.name: The window of the to-beginning-of-fiscal-year date scope
records.purpose: Reads everything that happened before the current fiscal year started, which is how the unallocated earnings of the previous years are shown on the balance sheet.

operands.name: the from-date of the requested period
operands.source: the date option of the rendering
operands.constraints: equal to the to-date for a single-date report

operands.name: the to-date of the requested period
operands.source: the date option of the rendering
operands.constraints: not before the from-date

operands.name: the fiscal year containing the to-date
operands.unit_or_currency: a first day and a last day
operands.source: the company's fiscal-year-end day and month, and the declared fiscal year records where they exist
operands.constraints: for a company closing on the thirty-first of December, the fiscal year containing a date in 2026 runs from the first of January 2026 to the thirty-first of December 2026

operands.name: whether the account carries forward
operands.source: the account
operands.constraints: evaluated per account

preconditions.condition: The from-date is not after the to-date.
preconditions.otherwise: The period is empty and every ledger figure is zero; a rebuild should refuse the option rather than render zeros.

preconditions.condition: The fiscal-year boundaries of the company are known.
preconditions.otherwise: The default rule of the last day and month applies, and a fiscal year shorter or longer than twelve months is taken from the declared fiscal year records.

procedure: Take the first day of the fiscal year containing the to-date and subtract one day: that is the upper bound.
Leave the lower bound open for an account that carries forward.
For an account that does not carry forward, set the lower bound to the first day of the fiscal year containing the upper bound, which is the previous fiscal year.
Note that the window therefore excludes the first day of the current fiscal year, because one day has already been subtracted.
records.formula:
upper_bound = fiscal_year_start − 1 day
lower_bound = none                                                  when the account carries forward
lower_bound = start of the fiscal year containing the upper bound   when the account does not carry forward

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded: the result is a pair of dates.
rounding.precision: Whole days.
rounding.step: No rounding step; both bounds are inclusive as written.

result.name: the window of the expression, per account
result.unit_or_currency: a first day, possibly open, and a last day, inclusive
result.stored_or_displayed: Not displayed; it is conjoined with the base restriction by every ledger-reading engine.

edge_cases.case: An income or expense account.
edge_cases.outcome: Its window ends before its own fiscal year starts, so the window is empty and the figure is zero.

edge_cases.case: An asset or liability account.
edge_cases.outcome: The window accumulates every movement up to the day before the current fiscal year began.

edge_cases.case: The report date falls in the first fiscal year of the company.
edge_cases.outcome: There is nothing before it and the figure is zero.

worked_examples.description: A line with this scope over the second quarter of a calendar fiscal year
worked_examples.narrative: The upper bound is the thirty-first of December of the previous year; an income account's own correction would start it on the first of January of the current year, which is after that bound, so its window is empty.

records.name: The window of the to-beginning-of-period date scope
records.purpose: Reads everything that happened before the requested period started, which is the initial balance column of the general ledger and of the trial balance.

operands.name: the from-date of the requested period
operands.source: the date option of the rendering
operands.constraints: equal to the to-date for a single-date report

operands.name: the to-date of the requested period
operands.source: the date option of the rendering
operands.constraints: not before the from-date

operands.name: the fiscal year containing the to-date
operands.unit_or_currency: a first day and a last day
operands.source: the company's fiscal-year-end day and month, and the declared fiscal year records where they exist
operands.constraints: for a company closing on the thirty-first of December, the fiscal year containing a date in 2026 runs from the first of January 2026 to the thirty-first of December 2026

operands.name: whether the account carries forward
operands.source: the account
operands.constraints: evaluated per account

preconditions.condition: The from-date is not after the to-date.
preconditions.otherwise: The period is empty and every ledger figure is zero; a rebuild should refuse the option rather than render zeros.

preconditions.condition: The fiscal-year boundaries of the company are known.
preconditions.otherwise: The default rule of the last day and month applies, and a fiscal year shorter or longer than twelve months is taken from the declared fiscal year records.

procedure: Take the from-date of the requested period and subtract one day: that is the upper bound.
Leave the lower bound open for an account that carries forward.
For an account that does not carry forward, set the lower bound to the first day of the fiscal year containing the upper bound.
Note that the window therefore excludes the from-date itself.
records.formula:
upper_bound = date_from − 1 day
lower_bound = none                                                  when the account carries forward
lower_bound = start of the fiscal year containing the upper bound   when the account does not carry forward

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded: the result is a pair of dates.
rounding.precision: Whole days.
rounding.step: No rounding step; both bounds are inclusive as written.

result.name: the window of the expression, per account
result.unit_or_currency: a first day, possibly open, and a last day, inclusive
result.stored_or_displayed: Not displayed; it is conjoined with the base restriction and it produces the initial balance figures.

edge_cases.case: A single-date report.
edge_cases.outcome: The window ends the day before that date.

edge_cases.case: An income or expense account whose period starts inside the fiscal year.
edge_cases.outcome: The window runs from the first day of that fiscal year to the day before the period.

edge_cases.case: The period starts on the first day of the fiscal year.
edge_cases.outcome: The upper bound is the last day of the previous fiscal year, and an income account's window is empty.

worked_examples.description: A line with this scope over the second quarter of a calendar fiscal year
worked_examples.narrative: One day is subtracted from the first of April, giving the thirty-first of March; the income account starts at the first of January by the carry-forward correction.

records.name: The window of the previous return period date scope
records.purpose: Widens the window to the whole tax return period immediately before the one containing the report date, which is the mechanism that lets a carry-over written on the last day of a period be read by the next one.

operands.name: the from-date of the requested period
operands.source: the date option of the rendering
operands.constraints: equal to the to-date for a single-date report

operands.name: the to-date of the requested period
operands.source: the date option of the rendering
operands.constraints: not before the from-date

operands.name: the fiscal year containing the to-date
operands.unit_or_currency: a first day and a last day
operands.source: the company's fiscal-year-end day and month, and the declared fiscal year records where they exist
operands.constraints: for a company closing on the thirty-first of December, the fiscal year containing a date in 2026 runs from the first of January 2026 to the thirty-first of December 2026

operands.name: the tax return periodicity of the company
operands.unit_or_currency: monthly, every two months, quarterly, every four months, twice a year, or yearly
operands.source: the company's tax return settings
operands.constraints: anchored on the company's fiscal year start

preconditions.condition: The from-date is not after the to-date.
preconditions.otherwise: The period is empty and every ledger figure is zero; a rebuild should refuse the option rather than render zeros.

preconditions.condition: The fiscal-year boundaries of the company are known.
preconditions.otherwise: The default rule of the last day and month applies, and a fiscal year shorter or longer than twelve months is taken from the declared fiscal year records.

preconditions.condition: The company's tax return periodicity is set.
preconditions.otherwise: The previous return period cannot be computed and no carry-over can be read back.

procedure: Find the tax return period containing the report's to-date, anchored on the company's fiscal year start.
Take the period immediately before it, of the same length.
Use its first day as the lower bound and its last day as the upper bound, both inclusive.
Apply no carry-forward correction: both bounds are set.
records.formula:
lower_bound = first day of the previous tax return period
upper_bound = last day of the previous tax return period

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded: the result is a pair of dates.
rounding.precision: Whole days.
rounding.step: No rounding step; both bounds are inclusive as written.

result.name: the window of the expression
result.unit_or_currency: a first day and a last day, both inclusive
result.stored_or_displayed: Not displayed; every shipped carry-in expression uses this scope so that the record written on the last day of the previous period falls inside its window.

edge_cases.case: The periodicity of the company changes while unconsumed carry-over records exist.
edge_cases.outcome: The meaning of the previous return period changes and a record can be orphaned; a rebuild should warn when the periodicity changes in that situation.

edge_cases.case: A period was skipped and never closed.
edge_cases.outcome: The chain is broken and the amount carried out of the skipped period is not picked up; the accountant must close the skipped period.

edge_cases.case: A company closes on the thirty-first of March with a quarterly periodicity.
edge_cases.outcome: The periods run from April to June, July to September, October to December and January to March, because the anchor is the fiscal year start.

worked_examples.description: A quarterly filer of a calendar fiscal year rendering a report with this scope
worked_examples.narrative: The fourteenth of August lies in the quarter from July to September, so the previous return period is the quarter from April to June.

worked_examples.description: The same scope in a report rendered for the second quarter
worked_examples.narrative: The containing period is the second quarter, so the window is the first quarter, for an asset account and for an income account alike.

records.name: The carry-forward correction of an unbounded window
records.purpose: Supplies the lower bound that the three unbounded date scopes leave open, per account, which is what makes one date scope serve both the balance sheet and the profit and loss statement.

operands.name: whether the account carries forward
operands.source: the account: true when its internal group is neither income nor expense and its type is not current-year earnings
operands.constraints: evaluated per account

operands.name: the upper bound of the window
operands.source: the date scope of the expression
operands.constraints: already computed

operands.name: the fiscal year containing the upper bound
operands.unit_or_currency: a first day and a last day
operands.source: the company's fiscal-year settings
operands.constraints: supplies the lower bound for an account that does not carry forward

preconditions.condition: The date scope is one of the three that leave the lower bound open.
preconditions.otherwise: The correction does not apply and the window's own lower bound is used.

preconditions.condition: The fiscal year containing the upper bound is known.
preconditions.otherwise: The default rule of the last day and month applies.

procedure: Determine whether the account carries forward: it does when its internal group is neither income nor expense and its type is not current-year earnings.
When it carries forward, leave the lower bound open, so the accumulation runs from the first entry ever posted.
When it does not carry forward, set the lower bound to the first day of the fiscal year containing the window's upper bound.
Apply the rule per account, not per expression, because one engine may read several accounts in the same pass.
records.formula:
effective_lower_bound = none                                                    when the account carries forward
effective_lower_bound = start of the fiscal year containing the upper bound      when the account does not carry forward

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded: the result is a pair of dates.
rounding.precision: Whole days.
rounding.step: No rounding step; both bounds are inclusive as written.

result.name: the effective lower bound, per account
result.unit_or_currency: a date or an open bound
result.stored_or_displayed: Not displayed; it completes the window every ledger-reading engine conjoins with the base restriction.

edge_cases.case: A balance sheet line and a profit and loss line share the from-beginning scope.
edge_cases.outcome: The balance sheet line accumulates all history and the profit and loss line accumulates only the fiscal year, with no change in the definition.

edge_cases.case: The current-year earnings account.
edge_cases.outcome: It does not carry forward, so it shows the result of the current fiscal year only.

edge_cases.case: An off-balance account.
edge_cases.outcome: Its internal group is neither income nor expense, so it carries forward.

edge_cases.case: The upper bound falls in an earlier fiscal year.
edge_cases.outcome: The lower bound is the start of that earlier fiscal year, not of the current one.

worked_examples.description: An income account read with the to-beginning-of-period scope over the second quarter of a calendar fiscal year
worked_examples.narrative: The upper bound of the thirty-first of March lies in the fiscal year beginning on the first of January, which becomes the lower bound.

worked_examples.description: An asset account read with the same scope
worked_examples.narrative: The account carries forward, so no lower bound is applied and the accumulation runs from the first entry ever posted.

records.name: The tax return period containing a date and the one before it
records.purpose: Locates the legal filing period a date falls in and the period immediately before it, which the previous return period scope and the carry-over mechanism both depend on.

operands.name: the to-date of the report
operands.source: the date option of the rendering
operands.constraints: the period containing it is sought

operands.name: the tax return periodicity
operands.unit_or_currency: monthly, every two months, quarterly, every four months, twice a year, or yearly
operands.source: the company's tax return settings
operands.constraints: one of the six

operands.name: the fiscal year start of the company
operands.source: the company's fiscal-year settings
operands.constraints: anchors where the periods begin

preconditions.condition: The periodicity of the company is one of the six.
preconditions.otherwise: No period can be computed.

preconditions.condition: The fiscal year start of the company is known.
preconditions.otherwise: The anchor is unknown and the periods cannot be aligned.

procedure: Anchor the sequence of return periods on the company's fiscal year start.
Find the period of the configured length that contains the report's to-date.
Take the period immediately before it, of the same length.
Return the first and the last day of that previous period.
records.formula:
containing_period  = the period of the configured length, anchored on the fiscal year start, that contains date_to
previous_period    = the period of the same length immediately before the containing period

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded: the result is a pair of dates.
rounding.precision: Whole days.
rounding.step: No rounding step; both bounds are inclusive as written.

result.name: the previous return period
result.unit_or_currency: a first day and a last day
result.stored_or_displayed: Not displayed; it is the window of every carry-in expression and the default date filter of the shipped tax reports.

edge_cases.case: A company closes on the thirty-first of March with a quarterly periodicity.
edge_cases.outcome: Its quarters run from April to June, July to September, October to December and January to March.

edge_cases.case: The periodicity is yearly.
edge_cases.outcome: The previous return period is the previous fiscal year.

edge_cases.case: The report's to-date is the first day of a period.
edge_cases.outcome: That period is the containing one and the previous period is the one that ended the day before.

worked_examples.description: A quarterly filer of a calendar fiscal year
worked_examples.narrative: The fourteenth of August lies in the third calendar quarter, so the previous return period runs from the first of April to the thirtieth of June.

worked_examples.description: A quarterly filer whose fiscal year starts on the first of April
worked_examples.narrative: The anchor moves the sequence to April, July, October and January, and the fourteenth of August still falls in the period from July to September.

records.name: The previous comparison period of a calendar period
records.purpose: Produces the comparison column of a period that is exactly a calendar unit, by shifting that unit back by one, so that a quarter is compared with a quarter and not with a span of ninety-one days.

operands.name: the from-date of the current period
operands.source: the date option
operands.constraints: must be the first day of a calendar month, quarter, half-year or year for this rule to apply

operands.name: the to-date of the current period
operands.source: the date option
operands.constraints: must be the last day of the same calendar unit

operands.name: the number of comparison periods
operands.source: the comparison option
operands.constraints: each further column shifts one more unit back

preconditions.condition: The period is exactly a calendar month, a calendar quarter, a calendar half-year or a calendar year.
preconditions.otherwise: The non-calendar rule applies instead and the comparison period is the same number of days immediately before the current period.

procedure: Recognise the calendar unit: the from-date is the first day of a calendar month, quarter, half-year or year and the to-date is the last day of that same unit.
Shift the whole unit back by one unit to obtain the first comparison period.
Shift again by one unit for each further comparison period requested.
Evaluate the whole pipeline once per comparison period, with only the date option replaced.
records.formula:
previous_period = the same calendar unit shifted back by one unit
for the n-th comparison column, the unit is shifted back n times

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded: the result is a pair of dates.
rounding.precision: Whole days.
rounding.step: No rounding step; the bounds are the first and the last day of the shifted unit.

result.name: the comparison period
result.unit_or_currency: a first day and a last day
result.stored_or_displayed: Not displayed as such; it becomes the date option of one further column group, whose header names the period.

edge_cases.case: A single-date report.
edge_cases.outcome: The comparison shifts the single date by the same rule with a zero-length period: the previous period is the same calendar unit ending one unit earlier.

edge_cases.case: The current period is a calendar year.
edge_cases.outcome: The comparison period is the previous calendar year.

edge_cases.case: Several comparison periods are requested.
edge_cases.outcome: Each is one unit earlier than the last.

edge_cases.case: Growth is enabled.
edge_cases.outcome: It appears only when exactly one comparison period is selected.

worked_examples.description: Two comparison periods on a calendar quarter
worked_examples.narrative: The quarter is shifted back one quarter to give the first comparison column and one quarter again to give the second.

records.name: The previous comparison period of a non-calendar period
records.purpose: Produces the comparison column of a period that is not a calendar unit, by taking the same number of days immediately before it, so that the two periods have the same length and do not overlap.

operands.name: the from-date of the current period
operands.source: the date option
operands.constraints: any date

operands.name: the to-date of the current period
operands.source: the date option
operands.constraints: not before the from-date

operands.name: the length of the current period
operands.source: computed from the two bounds
operands.constraints: at least one day

preconditions.condition: The period is not exactly a calendar month, quarter, half-year or year.
preconditions.otherwise: The calendar rule applies instead and the whole unit is shifted back by one unit.

procedure: Compute the length of the current period in days as the difference between the to-date and the from-date, plus one.
Set the comparison period's to-date to the day before the current from-date.
Set the comparison period's from-date to the current from-date less that many days.
Repeat from the comparison period for each further comparison column requested.
records.formula:
period_length_in_days = ( date_to − date_from ) + 1
previous_from         = date_from − period_length_in_days days
previous_to           = date_from − 1 day

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded: the result is a pair of dates.
rounding.precision: Whole days.
rounding.step: No rounding step; the length is a whole number of days by construction.

result.name: the comparison period
result.unit_or_currency: a first day and a last day
result.stored_or_displayed: Not displayed as such; it becomes the date option of one further column group.

edge_cases.case: The two periods must not overlap.
edge_cases.outcome: The comparison to-date is the day before the current from-date, which guarantees it.

edge_cases.case: The period is one day long.
edge_cases.outcome: The comparison period is the previous day.

edge_cases.case: The period spans a leap day.
edge_cases.outcome: The length in days already counts it, so the shifted period simply has the same number of days.

worked_examples.description: A thirty-day period that is not a calendar unit
worked_examples.narrative: The ninth of May minus the tenth of April, plus one, is thirty days; the comparison period ends on the ninth of April and starts thirty days before the tenth of April, that is on the eleventh of March.

records.name: The same period of the previous year
records.purpose: Produces the comparison column that answers how the same months of the previous year performed, by shifting both bounds back by exactly one year.

operands.name: the from-date of the current period
operands.source: the date option
operands.constraints: any date

operands.name: the to-date of the current period
operands.source: the date option
operands.constraints: not before the from-date

operands.name: the number of comparison periods
operands.source: the comparison option
operands.constraints: each further column shifts one more year back

preconditions.condition: Both bounds exist as dates one year earlier.
preconditions.otherwise: The twenty-ninth of February becomes the twenty-eighth of February in a year that is not a leap year.

procedure: Subtract one year from the from-date, keeping the day of the month.
Subtract one year from the to-date, keeping the day of the month.
Where the resulting day does not exist, use the twenty-eighth of February for a twenty-ninth of February.
Repeat for each further comparison column requested, one more year back each time.
records.formula:
previous_from = date_from − 1 year, keeping the day of the month
previous_to   = date_to   − 1 year, keeping the day of the month

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded: the result is a pair of dates.
rounding.precision: Whole days.
rounding.step: No rounding step; only the leap-day substitution applies.

result.name: the comparison period
result.unit_or_currency: a first day and a last day
result.stored_or_displayed: Not displayed as such; it becomes the date option of one further column group.

edge_cases.case: A leap-day bound shifted into a year that is not a leap year.
edge_cases.outcome: The twenty-ninth of February becomes the twenty-eighth.

edge_cases.case: Several comparison periods are requested.
edge_cases.outcome: Each is one further year back.

edge_cases.case: The period is a calendar quarter.
edge_cases.outcome: Both bounds still move by a year, not by four quarters, which is the same result for a calendar quarter.

worked_examples.description: One comparison against the same quarter of the previous year
worked_examples.narrative: Both bounds move back one year, keeping the day of the month.

worked_examples.description: A period ending on a leap day shifted into a year that is not a leap year
