worked_examples.narrative: The twenty-ninth of February does not exist in the earlier year and becomes the twenty-eighth.

records.name: The evaluation of a comparison column
records.purpose: States what changes and what does not when a further period column is rendered, so that a comparison column carries exactly the figures the report would show if that period were the current one.

operands.name: the shifted period
operands.unit_or_currency: a first day and a last day
operands.source: one of the shifting rules
operands.constraints: one per comparison column

operands.name: every other user option
operands.unit_or_currency: the option set of the rendering
operands.source: the user options
operands.constraints: unchanged from the current column

operands.name: the external values in the shifted window
operands.source: the stored external values
operands.constraints: selected in the shifted window, not in the current one

preconditions.condition: The comparison period is well formed.
preconditions.otherwise: The column cannot be evaluated and is not offered.

procedure: Replace only the date option with the shifted period.
Run the whole nine-step pipeline again with that option set.
Select the external values in the shifted window as well, so that a manual figure of the earlier period is shown in its own column.
Do not recompute the carry-over for a comparison column: closing a period is an action, not a rendering.
Place the resulting figures in their own column group, whose header names the period.
records.formula:
figures( comparison column ) = pipeline( report , options with date option replaced by the shifted period )
carry_over( comparison column ) = not recomputed

rounding.what: Nothing extra is rounded: each column is rounded exactly as the current column is.
rounding.precision: The decimal places of the presentation currency, and the report's whole-unit rounding when it sets one.
rounding.step: At display, per column.

result.name: the figures of the comparison column
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed in their own column group beside the current period's figures.

edge_cases.case: The comparison period was itself closed.
edge_cases.outcome: Its carry-over external values are read as ordinary external values, but no new carry-over is written.

edge_cases.case: The figures of a comparison column are compared with the report rendered for that period.
edge_cases.outcome: They must be equal, with the same filters: comparison is symmetric.

edge_cases.case: A single-date report is compared.
edge_cases.outcome: The single date is shifted by the same rule with a zero-length period.

worked_examples.description: A quarterly rendering with one comparison against the previous quarter
worked_examples.narrative: The pipeline runs once per column group and no carry-over record is written by the rendering, whichever column is being computed.

records.name: The growth percentage between two periods
records.purpose: Expresses the change between the current period and its single comparison period as a percentage, using the absolute value of the earlier figure so that a shrinking loss reads as an improvement.

operands.name: current value
operands.source: the figure of the expression in the current column
operands.constraints: any value

operands.name: comparison value
operands.source: the figure of the same expression in the comparison column
operands.constraints: any value; its absolute value is the denominator

preconditions.condition: Growth comparison is enabled on the report and exactly one comparison period is selected.
preconditions.otherwise: No growth column is produced at all.

preconditions.condition: The comparison value is not zero, or the current value is also zero.
preconditions.otherwise: The two special cases apply: an empty cell when both are zero, and the infinity marker when only the comparison value is zero.

procedure: When the comparison value is zero and the current value is zero, leave the growth cell empty.
When the comparison value is zero and the current value is not zero, show the infinity marker rather than a number, because the relative change is undefined.
Otherwise subtract the comparison value from the current value.
Divide by the absolute value of the comparison value, so that the direction of an improvement is preserved for negative figures.
Multiply by one hundred and round to one decimal place, half away from zero, then render with a trailing percent sign.
records.formula: growth_percentage = ( current_value − comparison_value ) ÷ | comparison_value | × 100

rounding.precision: One decimal place.
rounding.step: After the division and the multiplication by one hundred, immediately before rendering.

result.name: growth percentage
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed in the growth cell with a trailing percent sign, and painted favourable, unfavourable or neutral.

edge_cases.case: Both figures are zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The growth cell is empty.

edge_cases.case: The comparison figure is zero and the current figure is not.
edge_cases.outcome: The growth cell shows the infinity marker.

edge_cases.case: Both figures are negative and the current one is closer to zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The absolute value in the denominator makes the growth positive, which reads as the improvement it is.

edge_cases.case: The growth is exactly zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The cell is painted neutrally.

worked_examples.description: An income line that grew
worked_examples.narrative: One hundred and twenty-eight thousand four hundred less one hundred and twelve thousand, divided by one hundred and twelve thousand, times one hundred, is fourteen point six four two eight and so on, which rounds to fourteen point six percent.

worked_examples.description: A cost of revenue line that grew
worked_examples.narrative: Three thousand two hundred divided by fifty-eight thousand, times one hundred, is five point five one seven two and so on, which rounds to five point five percent.

worked_examples.description: A gross profit line that grew
worked_examples.narrative: Thirteen thousand two hundred divided by fifty-four thousand, times one hundred, is twenty-four point four four four and so on, which rounds to twenty-four point four percent.

worked_examples.description: A loss that shrank
worked_examples.narrative: Minus three thousand one hundred less minus eight thousand two hundred is five thousand one hundred; divided by the absolute value of eight thousand two hundred, times one hundred, that is sixty-two point one nine five and so on, which rounds to sixty-two point two percent.

worked_examples.description: A line that is zero in both periods and a line that appears from nothing
worked_examples.narrative: Both figures zero leaves the cell empty; a zero comparison against a non-zero current figure shows the infinity marker.

records.name: The favourable colour of a growth cell
records.purpose: Decides whether a change is painted as good or as bad, so that a fall in an expense reads as favourable and a fall in revenue does not.

operands.name: growth percentage
operands.source: the growth calculation
operands.constraints: may be positive, negative or zero

operands.name: the flag that says a positive change is good
operands.source: the expression of the line
operands.constraints: set so that a decrease reads as favourable on an expense line

preconditions.condition: A growth percentage was produced.
preconditions.otherwise: There is nothing to paint: an empty growth cell and the infinity marker carry the colour of the sign of the current figure only where the definition asks for it.

procedure: Read the growth percentage and the flag of the expression.
Paint the cell favourable when the growth is positive and the flag says a positive change is good, or when the growth is negative and the flag says a positive change is bad.
Paint the cell unfavourable in the two symmetric cases.
Paint a growth of exactly zero neutrally.
records.formula:
favourable = ( growth_percentage > 0 AND the flag says a positive change is good )
          OR ( growth_percentage < 0 AND the flag says a positive change is bad )

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded by the colour test.
rounding.precision: The growth percentage is already rounded to one decimal place.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, at the growth calculation.
rounding.step: After the growth percentage has been rounded.

result.name: the colour of the growth cell
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed as the colour of the growth cell.

edge_cases.case: An expense line.
edge_cases.outcome: Its flag says a positive change is bad, so a decrease is painted favourable.

edge_cases.case: An income line.
edge_cases.outcome: Its flag is left at the default, so an increase is painted favourable.

edge_cases.case: A growth of exactly zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The cell is painted neutrally, whatever the flag.

worked_examples.description: The four lines of the worked comparison
worked_examples.narrative: The income growth is positive on a line where a positive change is good, so it is favourable; the cost growth is positive on a line where a positive change is bad, so it is unfavourable; the shrinking loss reads positive on a line where a positive change is good, so it is favourable.

records.name: Whether a report line can be unfolded
records.purpose: Decides which lines offer sub-lines at all, which fixes what the unfold-all option expands and which lines the prefix-group and load-more rules can apply to.

operands.name: the child lines of the line
operands.source: the line tree of the definition
operands.constraints: any number, possibly none

operands.name: the grouping key of the line
operands.unit_or_currency: a list of field names, possibly empty
operands.source: the definition or the user
operands.constraints: an authored or a user grouping key both count

operands.name: whether the line is dynamically generated with sub-lines
operands.source: the generator of a dynamic report, such as the account lines of the general ledger or the partner lines of the partner ledger
operands.constraints: the generator declares whether the line has sub-lines

operands.name: the foldable flag
operands.source: the line
operands.constraints: when set, an unfoldable line starts folded

preconditions.condition: The line is rendered at all.
preconditions.otherwise: A line hidden by the hide-if-zero rule offers nothing, together with all of its descendants.

procedure: Answer yes when the line has child lines in the definition.
Answer yes when the line carries an authored or a user grouping key.
Answer yes when the line is dynamically generated and its generator declares sub-lines.
Answer no otherwise.
Expand an unfoldable line on opening unless its foldable flag is set, in which case start it folded; the unfold-all option expands every unfoldable line at once.
records.formula:
unfoldable( line ) = ( the line has child lines )
                  OR ( the line has an authored or a user grouping key )
                  OR ( the line is generated with sub-lines )

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded: the answer is a yes or no value.
rounding.precision: Not applicable.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: the line is unfoldable
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed as the presence of the fold marker on the row, and carried on the row as its foldable and unfolded flags.

edge_cases.case: A line has both children and a grouping key.
edge_cases.outcome: The definition refuses it: a line may not have both.

edge_cases.case: A line is collapsed and re-expanded.
edge_cases.outcome: The same sub-lines appear in the same order.

edge_cases.case: The unfold-all option is used on a very large ledger.
edge_cases.outcome: The prefix-group rule protects the rendering and the load-more limit still applies within each group.

worked_examples.description: A heading line with three children and no grouping key
worked_examples.narrative: The line has children, so it is unfoldable, and its foldable flag is not set, so it opens expanded.

worked_examples.description: A leaf line of a national return
worked_examples.narrative: None of the three tests succeeds, so the line offers no sub-lines.

records.name: The sub-lines of a grouped line
records.purpose: Splits the items a line matched into one sub-line per distinct value of the grouping key, with the line's own figures recomputed over each partition, so that a total can be read by partner, by account or by any other field of the item.

operands.name: the items the line's expressions matched
operands.unit_or_currency: items carrying amounts in the presentation currency
operands.source: the union over the line's expressions of the items each engine selected
operands.constraints: only ledger-reading engines contribute

operands.name: the grouping key
operands.unit_or_currency: a comma-separated list of field names of the Journal Item
operands.source: the definition or the user
operands.constraints: a field may be stored or derived, but a derived field must be non-stored and related, because grouping walks the relation at read time

operands.name: the ordering of the first key
operands.unit_or_currency: the display order of the linked records, or ascending value for a scalar
operands.source: the field itself
operands.constraints: fixes the order of the sub-lines

preconditions.condition: The line's expressions all use ledger-reading engines.
preconditions.otherwise: A line whose expression uses the aggregation engine or the external value engine cannot be grouped, and the definition forbids it.

preconditions.condition: The line has no child lines.
preconditions.otherwise: The definition refuses a line that has both children and a grouping key.

procedure: Take the union, over the line's expressions, of the Journal Items each engine selected.
Read the grouping key as an ordered list of field names of the Journal Item.
Partition the items by the tuple of those field values, in the order given.
Emit one sub-line per partition, in the order the first key's own ordering gives, named by the display name of the tuple, with the line's expressions re-evaluated over that partition only.
When the key list names more than one field, group the sub-lines again by the next key, producing one level per key.
records.formula:
sub_lines( line ) = one line per distinct tuple of the grouping key values among the matched items
figure( sub_line , expression ) = the expression re-evaluated over that partition only

rounding.what: Nothing extra is rounded: each sub-line is rounded exactly as any other line.
rounding.precision: The decimal places of the presentation currency, and the report's whole-unit rounding when it sets one.
rounding.step: At display, per sub-line; the partition sums are accumulated unrounded.

result.name: the sub-lines of the line
result.unit_or_currency: rows carrying figures in the presentation currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed beneath the line when it is unfolded; the sum of the sub-lines equals the line, up to rounding.

edge_cases.case: A partition would produce more sub-lines than the load-more limit.
edge_cases.outcome: The first sub-lines up to the limit are emitted with a continuation row.

edge_cases.case: A partition would produce more sub-lines than the prefix-group threshold.
edge_cases.outcome: One level of prefix groups is inserted instead, and that rule wins over the load-more limit.

edge_cases.case: A field of the key is derived.
edge_cases.outcome: It must be non-stored and related, because the grouping walks the relation when the items are read.

edge_cases.case: Eighty-six shipped report lines carry an authored grouping key.
edge_cases.outcome: They are grouped without the user asking.

worked_examples.description: A line matching six items grouped by partner
worked_examples.narrative: The six items fall into three partner partitions whose totals are four thousand two hundred, one thousand eight hundred and fifty and nine hundred and ninety, and their sum of seven thousand and forty equals the line.

worked_examples.description: The same line grouped by partner and then by account
worked_examples.narrative: The first key gives three sub-lines and the second key splits them into five, one level per key.

records.name: The load-more limit of an expansion
records.purpose: Caps how many sub-lines an expansion emits at once and offers the rest on demand, so that a line with very many sub-lines can still be opened.

operands.name: the number of candidate sub-lines
operands.source: the grouping or the generator of the line
operands.constraints: may be very large

operands.name: the load-more limit of the report
operands.source: the report definition
operands.constraints: zero or empty disables the mechanism

operands.name: the offset reached
operands.source: the rows already emitted
operands.constraints: starts at zero

preconditions.condition: The load-more limit is set and greater than zero.
preconditions.otherwise: The mechanism is disabled and every candidate sub-line is emitted.

preconditions.condition: The expansion does not exceed the prefix-group threshold.
preconditions.otherwise: The prefix-group rule wins: the candidates are grouped first and the load-more limit then applies to the prefix-group rows.

procedure: Emit the first sub-lines, in order, up to the load-more limit.
Emit one extra row of a special kind carrying the offset reached and the number of candidates remaining.
When the user activates that row, produce the next sub-lines starting at the offset, up to the limit again, and replace the row.
Repeat until no candidate remains.
records.formula:
rows_emitted        = min( number_of_candidates , load_more_limit )
remaining           = number_of_candidates − rows_emitted
continuation_row    = one row when remaining > 0, carrying the offset reached and the number remaining

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded: the figures are unchanged and only the number of rows is limited.
rounding.precision: Not applicable.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: the emitted sub-lines and the continuation row
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed beneath the expanded line; the figures of the line itself are unaffected by the limit.

edge_cases.case: The limit is zero or empty.
edge_cases.outcome: The mechanism is disabled and every sub-line is emitted.

edge_cases.case: The number of candidates equals the limit exactly.
edge_cases.outcome: No continuation row is emitted, because nothing remains.

edge_cases.case: Both the load-more limit and the prefix-group threshold would apply.
edge_cases.outcome: The prefix-group rule wins and the limit then applies to the prefix-group rows.

worked_examples.description: An account with two hundred and fifty items and a limit of eighty
worked_examples.narrative: Eighty rows are emitted and one continuation row says that the offset reached is eighty and that one hundred and seventy remain.

worked_examples.description: The same expansion after the continuation row has been activated twice
worked_examples.narrative: The third batch takes the rows from the offset of one hundred and sixty, leaving ten to load.

records.name: The prefix length of a prefix group
records.purpose: Chooses how many leading characters group the candidates of a very large expansion, so that a ledger of many thousands of accounts is navigated through a few levels rather than one endless list.

operands.name: the grouping string of each candidate
operands.source: the account code for an account line, the partner's display name for a partner line, the entry's number for an entry line
operands.constraints: one per candidate

operands.name: the number of candidates
operands.source: the expansion
operands.constraints: compared against the threshold

operands.name: the prefix-group threshold of the report
operands.source: the report definition, four thousand by default
operands.constraints: an expansion at or below it is not grouped

preconditions.condition: The number of candidates exceeds the prefix-group threshold.
preconditions.otherwise: The candidates are emitted directly, subject to the load-more limit.

preconditions.condition: At least two candidates have different grouping strings.
preconditions.otherwise: No prefix length yields more than one group and the candidates are emitted directly.

procedure: Compute the grouping string of every candidate.
Start with a prefix length of one.
Group the candidates by their first characters of that length and count the distinct groups.
Increase the length by one and repeat while the count of distinct groups is one.
Stop at the shortest length that yields more than one group, and emit one prefix-group row per distinct prefix, named after the prefix followed by an ellipsis, ordered by the prefix.

Make each prefix-group row unfoldable and repeat the whole rule on its own candidates when it is expanded; a prefix group whose candidate count is at or below the threshold expands directly into its candidates.
records.formula:
k = the smallest length ≥ 1 such that the number of distinct first-k-character prefixes among the candidates > 1
prefix_group_rows = one row per distinct prefix of length k, ordered by the prefix

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded by the grouping.
rounding.precision: Not applicable.
rounding.step: The figures of the prefix-group rows are computed after the grouping, by re-evaluating the line's expressions.

result.name: the prefix length and the prefix-group rows
result.unit_or_currency: a count of characters, and rows
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed as an intermediate level of rows named after the prefix followed by an ellipsis.

edge_cases.case: Every candidate shares the first three characters.
edge_cases.outcome: The prefix length grows to four before more than one group appears.

edge_cases.case: A prefix group still exceeds the threshold when expanded.
edge_cases.outcome: The rule is applied again on its own candidates, producing a further level.

edge_cases.case: A prefix group is at or below the threshold.
edge_cases.outcome: It expands directly into its candidates.

edge_cases.case: Both the prefix-group rule and the load-more limit would apply.
edge_cases.outcome: The prefix-group rule wins and the limit then applies to the prefix-group rows.

worked_examples.description: Six thousand account lines whose codes all start with the same digit
worked_examples.narrative: One character yields a single group, so the length grows to two, which yields nine distinct prefixes and therefore nine prefix-group rows.

worked_examples.description: An expansion below the threshold
worked_examples.narrative: The candidate count does not exceed the threshold, so the candidates are emitted directly.

records.name: The figures of a prefix-group row
records.purpose: Gives a prefix-group row its amounts by re-evaluating the line's expressions over the candidates it covers, so that an intermediate navigation level never introduces a rounding error.

operands.name: the candidates of the prefix group
operands.source: the grouping by prefix
operands.constraints: the candidates whose grouping string starts with that prefix

operands.name: the expressions of the line
operands.source: the report definition
operands.constraints: re-evaluated restricted to those candidates

preconditions.condition: The prefix group covers at least one candidate.
preconditions.otherwise: No row is emitted for an empty prefix.

procedure: Restrict the line's expressions to the candidates the prefix group covers.
Re-evaluate each expression over that restriction, accumulating at full stored precision.
Do not add the rounded figures of the candidates: the row is computed, not summed from displayed numbers.
Round once, at display.
records.formula:
figure( prefix_group_row , expression ) = the expression re-evaluated over the candidates of the prefix group
                                        ≠ Σ of the rounded figures of those candidates

rounding.what: The figure of the prefix-group row.
rounding.precision: The decimal places of the presentation currency, and the report's whole-unit rounding when it sets one.
rounding.step: Once, at display, after the re-evaluation.

result.name: figure of the prefix-group row
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed on the intermediate row; the sum of a line's sub-lines equals the line, up to rounding.

edge_cases.case: The report sets whole-unit rounding.
edge_cases.outcome: The prefix-group figure may differ from the sum of the rounded candidate figures, which is correct.

edge_cases.case: A prefix group is expanded into further prefix groups.
edge_cases.outcome: Each level is computed the same way, from the candidates and not from the level below.

worked_examples.description: A prefix group covering three accounts under whole-unit rounding
worked_examples.narrative: The three candidates each display ten, but the group is computed from thirty-one point two and displays thirty-one, which ties to the ledger where adding the rounded rows would not.

records.name: Hiding a line whose every cell rounds to zero
records.purpose: Removes the empty lines of a statement after rounding, so that a chart of accounts with hundreds of unused accounts still prints a readable report.

operands.name: the cells of the line
operands.source: the evaluation of the line's expressions for every column of every column group
operands.constraints: all of them are tested

operands.name: the hide-if-zero flag of the line
operands.source: the report definition
operands.constraints: when set, the line hides itself

operands.name: the report-level hide-zero option
operands.source: the user options
operands.constraints: when on, the test applies to every line whatever its flag

preconditions.condition: The line has been evaluated and rounded.
preconditions.otherwise: The test cannot run: it is deliberately made after evaluation and after rounding.

procedure: Evaluate the line and round every cell of every column of every column group.
When the hide-if-zero flag is set on the line and every one of those cells is zero after rounding, omit the line together with all of its descendants.
When the report-level hide-zero option is on, apply the same test to every line, whatever its flag.
When the report-level option is on, also hide a parent whose every descendant is hidden.
records.formula:
hidden( line ) = ( hide_if_zero_flag OR report_hide_zero_option )
             AND ( every rounded cell of every column group of the line = 0 )
hidden( parent ) = the report hide-zero option is on AND every descendant is hidden

rounding.what: The cells of the line, before the test.
rounding.precision: The decimal places of the presentation currency, and the report's whole-unit rounding when it sets one.
rounding.step: The test runs after evaluation and after rounding, so a line whose true value is four thousandths with a two-decimal presentation is hidden.

result.name: the line is hidden
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed as the absence of the row; the figures of the other lines are unchanged.

edge_cases.case: A line's true value is four thousandths with a two-decimal presentation.
edge_cases.outcome: It rounds to zero and the line is hidden.

edge_cases.case: A line has a non-zero cell in a comparison column only.
edge_cases.outcome: It is not hidden, because every cell of every column group must be zero.

edge_cases.case: A parent has only hidden descendants but its own cells are non-zero.
edge_cases.outcome: It is hidden only by the report-level option's parent rule, and that rule hides the parent whose every descendant is hidden.

edge_cases.case: The hide-if-zero flag is not set and the report-level option is off.
edge_cases.outcome: The line is shown, zeros included.

worked_examples.description: A line whose only figure is four thousandths, with the flag set
worked_examples.narrative: The cell rounds to zero at two decimal places, so the line and all of its descendants are omitted.

worked_examples.description: The same line with a non-zero comparison cell
worked_examples.narrative: Not every cell of every column group is zero, so the line is shown.

records.name: Sorting the rows of a sortable column
records.purpose: Reorders the rows of a statement by the figures of one column without breaking the tree, so that the largest balances can be found while every child stays under its parent.

operands.name: the cells of the sorted column
operands.source: the evaluation of the rows
operands.constraints: an empty cell is possible

operands.name: the sibling sets of the row tree
operands.source: the assembled rows
operands.constraints: sorting happens inside a sibling set only

operands.name: the sort direction
operands.source: the user
operands.constraints: chosen by clicking the column header

preconditions.condition: The column is marked sortable in the definition.
preconditions.otherwise: No sorting is offered on that column.

procedure: Sort only within each set of siblings, so that a child never moves out from under its parent.
Place the rows whose cell in that column is empty last, in both directions.
Keep the sort stable, so that rows with equal values keep their definition order.
Exclude the total lines, that is the lines whose expression aggregates over their siblings, and keep them in their defined position.
records.formula:
order( siblings ) = the siblings sorted by their cell in the sorted column, in the chosen direction,
                    with empty cells last in both directions, stable on ties,
                    and with the total lines held in their defined position

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded by the sort; the rounded figures are compared.
rounding.precision: The decimal places of the presentation currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, at display.
rounding.step: The sort runs after the cells have been assembled and rounded.

result.name: the ordered rows
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed in the new order; no figure changes.

edge_cases.case: Two rows have equal figures.
edge_cases.outcome: They keep their definition order, because the sort is stable.

edge_cases.case: A row has an empty cell in the sorted column.
edge_cases.outcome: It sorts last, whichever direction was chosen.

edge_cases.case: A total line aggregates over its siblings.
edge_cases.outcome: It is excluded from the sort and stays where the definition puts it.

edge_cases.case: A parent sorts after its former successor.
edge_cases.outcome: Its children move with it, because sorting happens inside a sibling set.

worked_examples.description: Four sibling account rows sorted descending on the balance column, one of them with an empty cell
worked_examples.narrative: The two equal figures keep their definition order, the smaller figure follows, and the row with the empty cell sorts last.

records.name: The coherence of the two prefixes of an account group
records.purpose: Completes a partly filled prefix range so that a group always has a starting prefix and an ending prefix of the same length, which the matching rule depends on.

operands.name: starting prefix
operands.source: the account group
operands.constraints: may be empty before the rule runs

operands.name: ending prefix
operands.source: the account group
operands.constraints: may be empty before the rule runs

preconditions.condition: At least one of the two prefixes is set.
preconditions.otherwise: The group has no range and matches no account.

preconditions.condition: The two prefixes have the same number of characters after the rule has run.
preconditions.otherwise: The stored check refuses the record with the message "The length of the starting and the ending code prefix must be the same".

procedure: When the ending prefix is empty, or the starting prefix is set and the ending prefix sorts before it, set the ending prefix to the starting prefix.
When the starting prefix is empty, or the ending prefix is set and the starting prefix sorts after it, set the starting prefix to the ending prefix.
Check that the two prefixes have the same number of characters and refuse the record otherwise.
Build the display name: the starting prefix alone when the two prefixes are equal, and otherwise the starting prefix, a hyphen and the ending prefix, followed by the group's name.

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded: the result is a pair of texts.
rounding.precision: Not applicable.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: the coherent prefix range and the display name
result.unit_or_currency: a pair of code prefixes and a text
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the account group and displayed as the name of the group line in the hierarchy.

edge_cases.case: Only the starting prefix is typed.
edge_cases.outcome: The ending prefix is set equal to it and the display name is the single prefix followed by the name.

edge_cases.case: The ending prefix sorts before the starting prefix.
edge_cases.outcome: The ending prefix is replaced by the starting prefix.

edge_cases.case: The two prefixes have different lengths after the rule.
edge_cases.outcome: The record is refused with the message about the length of the starting and the ending code prefix.

edge_cases.case: A group is deleted.
edge_cases.outcome: Its child groups are deleted with it, because the parent link cascades; the accounts are untouched and fall back to the next matching group or to the top level.

worked_examples.description: A group typed with a starting prefix only
worked_examples.narrative: The empty ending prefix is set to the starting prefix and the display name carries the single prefix.

worked_examples.description: A group whose two prefixes are typed in the wrong order
worked_examples.narrative: The ending prefix sorts before the starting prefix, so it is replaced by the starting prefix and the range becomes a single prefix.

worked_examples.description: A group with a genuine range
worked_examples.narrative: Both prefixes are set, of the same length and in order, so the range is kept and the display name carries both separated by a hyphen.

records.name: Matching an account to its account group
records.purpose: Places every account line under the most specific group whose prefix range contains its code, which is what the hierarchy filter renders instead of a flat list of accounts.

operands.name: the account code
operands.source: the account, as seen by the selected company
operands.constraints: compared as text

operands.name: the prefix range of each group
operands.unit_or_currency: a starting prefix and an ending prefix of equal length
operands.source: the account groups of the selected companies
operands.constraints: coherent by the completion rule

operands.name: the length of the group's prefixes
operands.source: the group
operands.constraints: fixes how many characters of the code are compared

preconditions.condition: At least one group's range contains the code.
preconditions.otherwise: The account line stays at the top level, after the groups.

procedure: Collect the accounts the report produced lines for.
For each account, take the first characters of its code, as many as the group's prefixes are long.
Keep a group when its starting prefix is less than or equal to those characters and its ending prefix is greater than or equal to them.
When several groups match, keep the one with the longest prefixes, that is the most specific group.
Emit one line per matched group, ordered by starting prefix, carrying the group's display name, and nest each group under its parent group recursively.
Attach each account line under its matched group, and leave the accounts that match no group at the top level, after the groups.
records.formula:
matched_group( account ) = the group with the longest prefixes among those where
                            starting_prefix ≤ first n characters of the code ≤ ending_prefix,
                            n being the length of that group's prefixes

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded by the matching.
rounding.precision: Not applicable.
rounding.step: The figures of the group lines are computed after the matching.

result.name: the group each account line hangs under
result.unit_or_currency: an account group or the top level
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed as the nesting of the rendered rows when the hierarchy filter is on.

edge_cases.case: Two groups match the same account.
edge_cases.outcome: The one with the longer prefixes wins, because it is the more specific.

edge_cases.case: No group matches.
edge_cases.outcome: The account line stays at the top level, after the groups.

edge_cases.case: A chart has several levels of groups.
edge_cases.outcome: Each group is nested under its parent recursively, producing several levels of lines.

edge_cases.case: Groups are ordered by starting prefix.
edge_cases.outcome: The hierarchy reads in chart order.

worked_examples.description: An account matched by a two-character group and a four-character group
worked_examples.narrative: Both ranges contain the code, but the group whose prefixes are four characters long is the more specific and takes the account.

worked_examples.description: An account outside every range
worked_examples.narrative: No range contains the code, so the account line stays at the top level.

records.name: The figures of an account group line
records.purpose: Gives a group line its amounts by recomputing over the accounts it contains, so that the hierarchy never introduces a rounding difference between a group and its accounts.

operands.name: the accounts contained by the group
operands.source: the matching rule, including the accounts of its child groups
operands.constraints: at least one

operands.name: the expressions of the report line
operands.source: the report definition
operands.constraints: re-evaluated restricted to those accounts

preconditions.condition: The group contains at least one account with a line.
preconditions.otherwise: No group line is emitted.

procedure: Determine the accounts the group contains, directly and through its child groups.
Re-evaluate the line's expressions restricted to those accounts, accumulating at full stored precision.
Do not add the rounded figures of the account lines.
Round once, at display.
records.formula:
figure( group_line , expression ) = the expression re-evaluated over the accounts the group contains
                                  ≠ Σ of the rounded figures of those account lines

rounding.what: The figure of the group line.
rounding.precision: The decimal places of the presentation currency, and the report's whole-unit rounding when it sets one.
rounding.step: Once, at display, after the re-evaluation.

result.name: figure of the group line
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed on the group row; the sum of a group's accounts equals the group, up to rounding.

edge_cases.case: The report sets whole-unit rounding.
edge_cases.outcome: The group figure may differ from the sum of the rounded account figures, which is correct.

edge_cases.case: A group has child groups.
edge_cases.outcome: Its figure covers the accounts of the child groups too, because it is recomputed over everything it contains.

edge_cases.case: A group's accounts are all hidden by the hide-if-zero rule.
edge_cases.outcome: The group's own figure is zero after rounding and the group is hidden with them when the option applies.

worked_examples.description: A group containing three accounts under whole-unit rounding
worked_examples.narrative: The group is computed from thirty-one point two and displays thirty-one, while the three accounts each display ten.

records.name: Filtering the rendered rows by the search text
records.purpose: Hides the rows that do not match a free-text search while keeping the tree navigable, and deliberately leaves every figure untouched.

operands.name: the search text
operands.source: the search box of the rendered report
operands.constraints: matched case-insensitively and accent-insensitively

operands.name: the name of each rendered line
operands.source: the assembled rows
operands.constraints: the only field matched

operands.name: the descendants of each line
operands.source: the row tree
operands.constraints: a line matches when any descendant matches

preconditions.condition: The report's search-bar flag is set.
preconditions.otherwise: No search box is offered and every row is shown.

procedure: Match the text against each line's name, ignoring case and ignoring accents.
Treat a line as matching when its own name matches or when any of its descendants match.
Show a matching line together with its whole ancestor chain, so that the tree stays navigable.
Do not recompute any figure: the search hides rows, it changes no total.
records.formula:
shown( line ) = ( the line's name matches the text )
             OR ( a descendant of the line matches )
             OR ( a descendant that matches has this line in its ancestor chain )
figures are unchanged by the search

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded and nothing is recomputed.
rounding.precision: Not applicable.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: the shown rows
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed; a total line keeps showing the total of everything, not of the visible rows.

edge_cases.case: A total line does not match the text.
edge_cases.outcome: It is still shown when a descendant matches, and it keeps the total of everything.

edge_cases.case: The text matches an accented name typed without accents.
edge_cases.outcome: It matches, because the comparison ignores accents.

edge_cases.case: No line matches.
edge_cases.outcome: No row is shown, and the figures of the report are still the figures of the whole report.

worked_examples.description: A search over a statement of forty rows
worked_examples.narrative: Three rows match by name and their four distinct ancestors are shown with them, and no total is recomputed.

records.name: The contribution of an item under the analytic filter
records.purpose: States that the analytic filter selects whole items rather than a share of them, which is the difference between reading the ledger and reading analytic lines.

operands.name: the analytic distribution of the item
operands.unit_or_currency: a set of analytic accounts with percentages
operands.source: the Journal Item
operands.constraints: a percentage may be any share

operands.name: the selected analytic accounts
operands.source: the analytic option
operands.constraints: empty means no restriction

operands.name: the selected analytic plans
operands.source: the analytic option
operands.constraints: empty means no restriction

operands.name: the balance of the item
operands.source: the Journal Item
operands.constraints: the whole balance is contributed

preconditions.condition: At least one analytic account or one analytic plan is selected.
preconditions.otherwise: No analytic condition is added and every item passes.

procedure: Keep the item when its analytic distribution names at least one of the selected analytic accounts, with any percentage.
Keep the item when its analytic distribution names at least one account belonging to one of the selected analytic plans.
When both selections are set, require the item to satisfy both.
Contribute the item's whole balance, never a percentage of it.
records.formula:
contribution( item ) = item_balance    when the analytic distribution names a selected account or an account of a selected plan
contribution( item ) = 0                otherwise

rounding.what: Nothing extra is rounded: the whole balance enters the sum unrounded.
rounding.precision: The decimal places of the presentation currency at display.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, at display.
rounding.step: No rounding step is introduced by the filter.

result.name: the contribution of the item
result.stored_or_displayed: Not displayed on its own; it enters the sum of whichever engine reads the item.

edge_cases.case: An item assigns thirty percent of its distribution to a selected account.
edge_cases.outcome: It contributes its whole balance, not thirty percent of it.

edge_cases.case: Both an analytic account and an analytic plan are selected.
edge_cases.outcome: The item must satisfy both conditions.

edge_cases.case: A report must apportion by percentage.
edge_cases.outcome: It reads analytic lines instead of Journal Items, which is the reporting of the analytic accounting documents and not of this domain.

worked_examples.description: An item of one thousand two hundred whose distribution assigns thirty percent to a selected analytic account
worked_examples.narrative: The filter selects whole items, so the whole one thousand two hundred enters the figure and not the three hundred and sixty a proportional reading would give.

records.name: The conjunction of a saved journal-item filter
records.purpose: Adds a stored search over Journal Items to the base restriction, which lets a user narrow a whole statement by a condition the report's own options do not offer.

operands.name: the saved filter
operands.unit_or_currency: a stored search over Journal Items
operands.source: the saved searches of the application
operands.constraints: chosen by the user

operands.name: the base restriction
operands.source: the pipeline
operands.constraints: the filter is conjoined to it

preconditions.condition: The report's favourite-filters switch is on.
preconditions.otherwise: No saved filter may be chosen and the base restriction is unchanged.

procedure: Take the saved search the user chose.
Conjoin it to the base restriction, so that it narrows the item set for every ledger-reading engine at once.
Apply it even when it references a field the report's engines do not otherwise read.
Never apply it to the external value engine, which reads no Journal Item.
records.formula:
base_restriction_with_filter = base_restriction AND saved_filter
external value figures are unchanged by the saved filter

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded by the conjunction.
rounding.precision: Not applicable.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: the narrowed set of readable Journal Items
result.stored_or_displayed: Not displayed; every ledger figure of the rendering is computed over the narrowed set.

edge_cases.case: The saved filter references a field no engine of the report reads.
edge_cases.outcome: It is still applied and narrows the item set for every engine.

edge_cases.case: The report mixes ledger figures and external figures.
edge_cases.outcome: The ledger figures narrow and the external figures do not, so a total over both changes only by its ledger part.

edge_cases.case: No saved filter is chosen.
edge_cases.outcome: The base restriction is unchanged.

worked_examples.description: A statement whose ledger lines total sixty thousand narrowed by a saved filter that keeps two thirds of the items
worked_examples.narrative: The ledger figure falls to forty thousand while the external figure of two hundred and forty is untouched, because the saved filter is never applied to the external value engine.

records.name: The displayed figure of a line that carries over
records.purpose: Adds what an earlier period carried forward to what the period's own ledger activity produced, which is the figure a filer sees on a box subject to carry-over.

operands.name: own movement
operands.source: the period's own ledger activity for the line, normally a tax tag expression over the strict range
operands.constraints: may be positive or negative

operands.name: carried in
operands.source: the expression labelled with the applied-carry-over prefix, that is the sum of the carry-over external values whose date falls in its window
operands.constraints: zero when nothing was carried

operands.name: the displayed label
operands.source: the column of the report
operands.constraints: the column binds to this label, which is why the intermediate expressions are not shown

preconditions.condition: The line carries the three cooperating expressions: the displayed one, the carry-in one and the carry-out one.
preconditions.otherwise: There is no carry-over on that line and the displayed figure is the period's own movement alone.

preconditions.condition: The carry-in expression uses the previous return period scope.
preconditions.otherwise: The record written on the last day of the previous period falls outside the window and nothing is carried in.

procedure: Evaluate the period's own movement for the line.
Evaluate the carry-in expression, which reads the carry-over external values of the previous return period.
Add the two.
records.formula: displayed = own_movement + carried_in

rounding.precision: The decimal places of the presentation currency, and the number of decimals of a rounding clause when the expression carries one.
rounding.step: At display; the addition itself is exact over two stored figures.

result.name: displayed figure of the box
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed in the cell bound to the column's expression label, and read by the carry-out expression.

edge_cases.case: Nothing was carried in.
edge_cases.outcome: The displayed figure is the period's own movement.

edge_cases.case: The carried-in amount is negative.
edge_cases.outcome: It reduces the displayed figure, which is the whole purpose of the mechanism.

edge_cases.case: A period was skipped and never closed.
edge_cases.outcome: Nothing is carried in, because the chain is broken; the accountant must close the skipped period.

edge_cases.case: No Journal Entry is created by the transfer.
edge_cases.outcome: The carry-over is a reporting fact, not an accounting fact.

worked_examples.description: A month whose own movement is negative and which carries nothing in
worked_examples.narrative: Minus four hundred and twenty plus zero is minus four hundred and twenty.

worked_examples.description: The following month, which carries the negative amount in
worked_examples.narrative: One thousand one hundred and thirty plus minus four hundred and twenty is seven hundred and ten.

records.name: The amount carried out of a period
records.purpose: Decides how much of the displayed figure must be transferred to the next period, which is what the bound clause on the carry-out expression exists to express.

operands.name: displayed figure
operands.source: the expression the column binds to, or an intermediate unbounded expression
operands.constraints: the figure the carry-out expression references

operands.name: the bound clause of the carry-out expression
operands.source: the report definition
operands.constraints: for example the clause that keeps a value only below zero, or the clause that clamps between zero and one hundred

preconditions.condition: The carry-out expression carries a bound clause.
preconditions.otherwise: Every period would carry its whole figure forward, which is not a carry-over but a duplication.

preconditions.condition: The carry-out expression's target resolves, explicitly or by the automatic rule.
preconditions.otherwise: The closing is refused because the carry-over target cannot be resolved.

procedure: Read the displayed figure, or the intermediate unbounded figure the carry-out expression references.
Apply the bound clause of the carry-out expression.
When the clause admits the figure, the carried-out amount is that figure.
When the clause rejects it, the carried-out amount is zero.
Remember the amount; write it only when the period is actually closed.
records.formula:
carried_out = displayed    when the bound clause admits it
carried_out = 0            otherwise

rounding.precision: The decimal places of the presentation currency, and the number of decimals of a rounding clause when the expression carries one.
rounding.step: Before the amount is written to an external value, so that what is carried is exactly what was shown.

result.name: carried-out amount
result.stored_or_displayed: Not normally displayed; it is written as a carry-over external value when the period is closed.

edge_cases.case: The period is only rendered, not closed.
edge_cases.outcome: The amount is computed and remembered but no record is written.

edge_cases.case: The clause rejects the figure.
edge_cases.outcome: Nothing is carried and the chain simply does not continue for that period.

edge_cases.case: The clause is the clamp between zero and one hundred.
edge_cases.outcome: Only a debt below one hundred is carried, and a larger debt is declared and paid.

edge_cases.case: The period is closed a second time.
edge_cases.outcome: The existing record is overwritten rather than doubled.

worked_examples.description: A month whose displayed figure is negative, with a clause that keeps a value only below zero

inputs.clause: keeps a value only below zero

worked_examples.narrative: Minus four hundred and twenty is below zero, so the whole negative position is carried out.

worked_examples.description: The following month, whose displayed figure is positive

inputs.clause: keeps a value only below zero

worked_examples.narrative: Seven hundred and ten is not below zero, so nothing is carried out.

records.name: The declared figure under the flooring in the definition
records.purpose: Floors the declared box at zero inside the report definition, which is the variant used where the law forbids a negative box outright, and which pairs a declared amount with a carried amount so that exactly one of the two is non-zero.

operands.name: displayed figure
operands.source: the sum of the period's own movement and the amount carried in
operands.constraints: may be positive or negative

operands.name: the clause on the declared expression
operands.unit_or_currency: the clause that keeps a value only above zero
operands.source: the report definition
operands.constraints: applied to the same underlying figure as the carry-out clause

operands.name: the clause on the carry-out expression
operands.unit_or_currency: the clause that keeps a value only below zero
operands.source: the report definition
operands.constraints: the complement of the declared clause

preconditions.condition: Both clauses read the same underlying figure.
preconditions.otherwise: The conservation property fails and an amount could be declared and carried at the same time, or neither.

procedure: Compute the displayed figure as the period's own movement plus the amount carried in.
Declare the figure when it is strictly above zero, and declare zero otherwise.
Carry the figure out when it is strictly below zero, and carry nothing otherwise.
Observe that exactly one of the two is non-zero in any period, because the two clauses are complementary at zero.
records.formula:
declared    = displayed    when displayed > 0
declared    = 0            when displayed ≤ 0
carried_out = displayed    when displayed < 0
carried_out = 0            when displayed ≥ 0

rounding.what: The declared figure and the carried amount.
rounding.precision: The decimal places of the presentation currency, and whole amounts where the legislation declares whole amounts.
rounding.step: After the bound clauses, at display and before the carry-over record is written.

result.name: declared figure and carried amount
result.stored_or_displayed: The declared figure is displayed and filed; the carried amount is written as a carry-over external value when the period is closed.

edge_cases.case: The displayed figure is exactly zero.
edge_cases.outcome: Neither clause admits it, so nothing is declared and nothing is carried.

edge_cases.case: Over a run of consecutive periods.
edge_cases.outcome: The sum of what was declared plus what is still carried equals the sum of the periods' own movements.

edge_cases.case: The carried amount is the net position.
edge_cases.outcome: It is not a second copy of an earlier amount, because the carry-in is already inside the displayed figure the carry-out is computed from.

worked_examples.description: A month declaring a box that the law forbids to be negative
worked_examples.narrative: The displayed figure of minus four hundred and twenty is not above zero, so zero is declared, and it is below zero, so the whole amount is carried.

worked_examples.description: The following month
worked_examples.narrative: Seven hundred and ten is above zero, so it is declared, and it is not below zero, so nothing is carried; the company has paid tax on one thousand one hundred and thirty less four hundred and twenty across the two months.

worked_examples.description: A third variant where the second month is also negative
worked_examples.narrative: One hundred and fifty plus minus four hundred and twenty is minus two hundred and seventy, so zero is declared and the net two hundred and seventy is carried into the next period.

records.name: The declared figure under the flooring in the filing format
records.purpose: Displays the unbounded figure, negative included, and leaves the flooring to the national filing format, which is the variant the incoming-operation boxes of the Belgian return use.

operands.name: displayed figure
operands.source: the sum of the period's own movement and the amount carried in, with no bound clause on the displayed expression
operands.constraints: may be negative

operands.name: the clause on the carry-out expression
operands.unit_or_currency: the clause that keeps a value only below zero
operands.source: the report definition
operands.constraints: the only bound clause of the pattern

operands.name: the filing format
operands.source: the country package
operands.constraints: writes zero to the legal file for a negative box

preconditions.condition: The displayed expression carries no bound clause.
preconditions.otherwise: The variant becomes the flooring in the definition instead.

preconditions.condition: The filing format floors the box at zero.
preconditions.otherwise: A negative amount would be filed, which the law forbids.

procedure: Compute the displayed figure as the period's own movement plus the amount carried in, with no bound clause.
Show the displayed figure as it stands, negative included.
Apply the bound clause on the carry-out expression only, so that a negative figure is carried out.
Let the national filing format write zero to the legal file, and let the next period pick the carried amount up.
records.formula:
displayed   = own_movement + carried_in            with no bound clause
carried_out = displayed    when displayed < 0
carried_out = 0            when displayed ≥ 0
filed       = 0            when displayed < 0, written by the filing format

rounding.what: The displayed figure and the carried amount.
rounding.precision: The decimal places of the presentation currency.
rounding.step: At display and before the carry-over record is written.

result.name: displayed figure, filed figure and carried amount
result.stored_or_displayed: The displayed figure is shown on screen, the filed figure is written by the national format, and the carried amount is written as a carry-over external value when the period is closed.

edge_cases.case: The six incoming-operation boxes of the Belgian return.
edge_cases.outcome: Each holds five expressions, of which only the displayed one is bound to the column; the other four are the raw tag total, the amount carried in, their sum and the amount to carry out.

edge_cases.case: A reader compares the screen with the legal file.
edge_cases.outcome: They differ for a negative box, which is intended by this variant.

edge_cases.case: The conservation property.
edge_cases.outcome: It is the same as in the other variant: declared plus still carried equals the sum of the own movements.

worked_examples.description: An incoming-operation box whose period movement is negative
worked_examples.narrative: The screen shows minus four hundred and twenty, the legal file receives zero and the whole amount is carried into the next period.

records.name: Writing the carry-over external value
records.purpose: Records, when a period is closed, what must be picked up by the next period, in a form the carry-in expression can read, and does so idempotently so that re-closing never doubles an amount.

operands.name: the carried-out amount
operands.source: the carry-out expression
operands.constraints: written only when it is not zero

operands.name: the target expression
operands.unit_or_currency: an expression of a report line
operands.source: the explicit carry-over target field, or the automatic rule that looks for the applied-carry-over label on the same line
operands.constraints: must resolve

operands.name: the last day of the period being closed
operands.source: the period of the closing
operands.constraints: the date written on the record

operands.name: the company being closed
operands.source: the closing
operands.constraints: one record per company

operands.name: the origin line and the origin expression label
operands.unit_or_currency: a report line and a label
operands.source: the carry-out expression
operands.constraints: they identify the record as a carry-over rather than a manual value

preconditions.condition: The period is actually being closed, that is a tax return is being validated.
preconditions.otherwise: Nothing is written: carry-over records are not written on every rendering.

preconditions.condition: The carry-out amount is not zero.
preconditions.otherwise: No record is written for that expression.

preconditions.condition: The carry-over target resolves.
preconditions.otherwise: The closing is refused because the carry-over target cannot be resolved.

procedure: For each carrying expression whose computed carry-out amount is not zero, determine the target expression, explicitly or by the automatic rule.

Create one external value carrying the target expression, the last day of the period being closed as its date, the company being closed, the carry-out amount as its value, the line the carry-out came from as its origin line, the carry-out expression's label as its origin expression label, and a name that states the origin line and the closed period.
When such a record already exists for the same target, date, company and origin, overwrite its value instead of creating a second one.
Write nothing at all when the report is merely rendered.
records.formula:
one external value per carrying expression with carried_out ≠ 0,
identified by ( target expression , last day of the closed period , company , origin line and label ),
value = carried_out ; an existing record with the same identity is overwritten

rounding.what: The carried-out amount, before it is written.
rounding.precision: The decimal places of the presentation currency, or the decimals of the expression's rounding clause.
rounding.step: Before the value is stored, so that what is stored is exactly what was shown.

result.name: carry-over external value
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored as an external value record with a non-empty origin line, which is what distinguishes it from a manual value; no Journal Entry is produced.

edge_cases.case: The period is closed a second time.
edge_cases.outcome: The existing record is overwritten, so the carry-over is never doubled.

edge_cases.case: The validation is cancelled or reset to draft.
edge_cases.outcome: The carry-over records written by that validation are deleted, so that re-closing produces the same figures from scratch.

edge_cases.case: The carry-out expression sits on a different line from the carry-in expression.
edge_cases.outcome: The explicit carry-over target is required, because the automatic rule looks on the same line only.

edge_cases.case: Two carry-overs run in parallel on one line.
edge_cases.outcome: Each has its own target and its own record, which is what the Italian monthly return does for a debt and for a credit.

worked_examples.description: Closing a month that carries a negative box forward
worked_examples.narrative: One external value of minus four hundred and twenty is written on the thirty-first of March, targeting the carry-in expression of the box, and no accounting entry is produced.

worked_examples.description: Re-closing the same month
worked_examples.narrative: The record of the same target, date, company and origin is found and overwritten, so the carried amount stays at minus four hundred and twenty.

records.name: Reading the carried-in amount back
records.purpose: Picks up, in the next period, the amount the previous closing wrote, by widening the window to the whole previous tax return period so that a record dated on the last day of that period falls inside it.

operands.name: the carry-over external values targeting this expression
operands.source: the stored external values
operands.constraints: selected for the selected companies

operands.name: the window of the previous return period
operands.unit_or_currency: a first day and a last day
operands.source: the previous return period date scope
operands.constraints: the record written on the last day of the previous period falls inside it

operands.name: the ordering
operands.unit_or_currency: date ascending, then stored identifier ascending
operands.source: the records
operands.constraints: the last record of the ordering is the one read

preconditions.condition: The carry-in expression is declared with the external value engine, the formula that takes the most recent value, no subformula and the previous return period date scope.
preconditions.otherwise: The record is not found: the record is dated inside the previous period and outside the current one, so the current period's own window would miss it.

preconditions.condition: The company's tax return periodicity has not changed since the record was written.
preconditions.otherwise: The meaning of the previous return period has changed and the record can be orphaned; a rebuild should warn when the periodicity changes while unconsumed carry-over records exist.

procedure: Take the carry-over external values whose target expression is this expression and whose company is one of the selected companies.
Keep those whose date falls between the first and the last day of the previous tax return period.
Order them by date ascending and then by stored identifier ascending.
Take the value of the last record, and take zero when no such record exists.
records.formula:
carried_in = value of the last carry-over external value v targeting this expression,
             for the selected companies,
             whose date falls in [ first day of the previous return period ,
                                   last day of the previous return period ],
             ordered by date then by identifier
carried_in = 0    when no such value exists

rounding.precision: The decimal places of the presentation currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, at display.
rounding.step: After the selection; the stored value is used as it stands.

result.name: carried-in amount
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed only through the figure that adds it to the period's own movement; the drill-down lists the external value record itself.

edge_cases.case: A second record exists for the same period.
edge_cases.outcome: The most recent one wins rather than both being added, which is why the formula takes the most recent value and not the sum.

edge_cases.case: A period was skipped and never closed.
edge_cases.outcome: Nothing is picked up: the amount is not silently accumulated and the accountant must close the skipped period.

edge_cases.case: The periodicity of the company changes.
edge_cases.outcome: The previous return period means something else and the record can be orphaned.

edge_cases.case: No record exists.
edge_cases.outcome: The carried-in amount is zero, not empty.

worked_examples.description: A monthly filer reading back the amount carried out of March, in April
worked_examples.narrative: The record of the thirty-first of March falls inside the previous return period, so April carries minus four hundred and twenty in.

worked_examples.description: The same filer in May, after April carried nothing out
worked_examples.narrative: No carry-over record falls in April, so May carries nothing in.

records.name: The presentation currency of a report
records.purpose: Fixes the one currency every figure of a rendering is expressed in, so that a consolidated statement over companies of different currencies is arithmetically meaningful.

operands.name: the ordered set of selected companies
operands.source: the company option, or the companies of the selected tax unit
operands.constraints: at least one; the order matters

operands.name: the currency of each selected company
operands.source: the company
operands.constraints: may differ between companies

preconditions.condition: At least one company is selected.
preconditions.otherwise: There is no presentation currency and nothing can be rendered.

procedure: Take the first company of the ordered selection.
Take its currency as the presentation currency of the whole rendering.
Convert every figure held in another currency into that currency before it is displayed and before it enters any aggregation.
records.formula:
presentation_currency = the currency of the first selected company
every figure is expressed in that currency before display and before any aggregation

rounding.precision: The decimal places of the presentation currency.
rounding.step: After the conversion and before the figure enters an aggregation.

result.name: the presentation currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed as the currency symbol of every monetary cell, and used as the currency of every bound of a subformula clause.

edge_cases.case: Every selected company shares one currency.
edge_cases.outcome: No conversion is needed.

edge_cases.case: Several companies with different currencies are selected.
edge_cases.outcome: Every figure is translated into the currency of the first selected company.

edge_cases.case: A bound of a subformula clause is written in another currency.
edge_cases.outcome: It is converted into the presentation currency before the bound test.

edge_cases.case: The order of the selection changes.
edge_cases.outcome: The presentation currency changes with it.

worked_examples.description: A consolidation of two companies, the first in euros and the second in another currency
worked_examples.narrative: The currency of the first selected company is the presentation currency, so every figure of the second company is converted into euros before it is displayed or aggregated.

records.name: Converting a foreign balance at the rate of the report date
records.purpose: Expresses balances held in another currency at the rate in force at the report's to-date, which is the mode that shows what a foreign holding is worth today.

operands.name: the balance held in another currency
operands.source: the Journal Items of that currency
operands.constraints: accumulated before conversion

operands.name: the rate in force at the report's to-date
operands.unit_or_currency: a rate between the two currencies
operands.source: the currency rates of the multi-currency documents
operands.constraints: the rate of the day of the to-date

operands.name: the presentation currency
operands.source: the currency of the first selected company
operands.constraints: the target of the conversion

preconditions.condition: The report's currency translation field is set to the mode that converts at the report date.
preconditions.otherwise: The other mode applies and the stored company-currency amounts are used as they stand.

preconditions.condition: A rate exists between the two currencies at the report's to-date.
preconditions.otherwise: The multi-currency documents specify the fallback to the most recent earlier rate.

procedure: Accumulate the balance in the currency it is held in.
Read the rate in force between that currency and the presentation currency on the report's to-date.
Multiply the balance by that rate.
Round to the decimal places of the presentation currency.
records.formula: converted_balance = foreign_balance × rate( foreign currency → presentation currency , report_date_to )

rounding.precision: The decimal places of the presentation currency.
rounding.step: After the multiplication by the rate, before the figure is displayed or aggregated.

result.name: converted balance
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed in the cell; the whole report moves when the rate moves, because every foreign balance is converted at the same date.

edge_cases.case: The rate changes.
edge_cases.outcome: The whole report changes with it, which is the defining property of this mode.

edge_cases.case: The balance is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The conversion leaves zero, whatever the rate.

edge_cases.case: The report is rendered for a past date.
edge_cases.outcome: The rate of that date is used, so the report is reproducible.

worked_examples.description: A foreign balance of ten thousand converted at a rate of nought point nine two two seven
worked_examples.narrative: Ten thousand times nought point nine two two seven is nine thousand two hundred and twenty-seven exactly at two decimal places.

records.name: Keeping a foreign balance at the rate it was recorded at
records.purpose: Uses the company-currency amount already stored on each Journal Item and presents the residual difference on a dedicated line, which is the mode that keeps a balance sheet in balance without touching the ledger.

operands.name: the company-currency amount stored on each Journal Item
operands.source: the Journal Item
operands.constraints: recorded at the rate of the day of the item

operands.name: the resulting asset total and liability total
operands.source: the report
operands.constraints: their difference is the translation adjustment

operands.name: the cumulative translation adjustment line
operands.source: the report definition
operands.constraints: carries the difference

preconditions.condition: The report's currency translation field is set to the mode that keeps the recorded rate.
preconditions.otherwise: The other mode applies and every foreign balance is converted at the report's to-date.

preconditions.condition: The report carries a cumulative translation adjustment line.
preconditions.otherwise: The difference has nowhere to go and the statement does not balance.

procedure: Use the company-currency amount already stored on each Journal Item as it stands, with no conversion.
Accumulate the figures of every line from those stored amounts.
Compute the difference that arises between the resulting asset total and the resulting liability and equity total.
Present that difference on the dedicated cumulative translation adjustment line.
records.formula:
line_figure           = Σ of the stored company-currency amounts, with no re-conversion
translation_adjustment = asset total − ( liability total + equity total )

rounding.what: The stored amounts are already rounded to the company currency.
rounding.precision: The decimal places of the presentation currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, at display.
rounding.step: No conversion step is introduced, so no rounding difference is introduced either.

result.name: the figures at their recorded rates and the translation adjustment
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed on the ordinary lines and on the cumulative translation adjustment line; the ledger is untouched.

edge_cases.case: A report inherits nothing and sets no translation mode.
edge_cases.outcome: This mode is the default, because it is the one that keeps a balance sheet in balance without touching the ledger.

edge_cases.case: The rate moves after the items were recorded.
edge_cases.outcome: The figures do not move, because the stored amounts are used as they stand.

edge_cases.case: The difference is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The adjustment line shows zero.

worked_examples.description: A balance sheet whose asset total and liability and equity total differ by the translation effect
worked_examples.narrative: Four hundred and twelve thousand three hundred less four hundred and ten thousand eight hundred and fifty is one thousand four hundred and fifty, which the cumulative translation adjustment line carries so that the statement balances.

records.name: The order in which a figure is rounded
records.purpose: Fixes the fixed sequence of rounding steps a figure passes through between the ledger and the screen, which is where independent rebuilds would otherwise diverge.

operands.name: the accumulated figure
operands.source: the engine that produced it
operands.constraints: accumulated at full stored precision

operands.name: the rounding clause of the expression
operands.unit_or_currency: a number of decimal places, when present
operands.source: the subformula
operands.constraints: either the clause of an aggregation expression or the clause of an external expression

operands.name: the report's whole-unit rounding mode
operands.unit_or_currency: one of the three modes, when the report sets one
operands.source: the report definition
operands.constraints: half away from zero, always away from zero, or always towards zero

operands.name: the presentation rounding unit
operands.source: the user options
operands.constraints: chosen by the reader

preconditions.condition: Intermediate sums were never rounded.
preconditions.otherwise: The figures diverge from the ledger and a total no longer ties.

procedure: Accumulate at full stored precision and never round an intermediate sum.
Apply the expression's own rounding when its subformula carries a number of decimal places.
Apply the report's whole-unit rounding when the report sets one, in the mode it names.
Apply the presentation rounding unit chosen by the reader, dividing by one for units, by one thousand for thousands and by one million for millions.
Format with the currency symbol at the position the currency declares, and the thousands separator and decimal separator of the reader's language.
records.formula:
step 1: accumulate at full precision
step 2: value = round( value , decimals of the expression's clause )        when it carries one
step 3: value_rounded = round_to_whole_unit( value , mode )                 when the report sets one
step 4: displayed = value_rounded ÷ scale
step 5: format with the currency symbol and the reader's separators

rounding.precision: First the decimals of the expression's clause when there is one, then the whole unit when the report sets one, then the rounding unit of the reader, which renders with the decimal places of the presentation currency for units and with one decimal for thousands and millions.
rounding.method: Half away from zero for the expression's clause, and the mode the report names for the whole-unit rounding.
rounding.step: In that order and no other: the report-level whole-unit rounding applies after any expression-level clause and before the presentation rounding unit.

result.name: displayed figure
result.unit_or_currency: the presentation currency, scaled by the rounding unit
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed in the cell, formatted with the currency symbol and the reader's separators.

edge_cases.case: An intermediate sum is rounded.
edge_cases.outcome: The result no longer ties to the ledger; this is forbidden.

edge_cases.case: The expression carries no rounding clause.
edge_cases.outcome: The second step is skipped.

edge_cases.case: The report sets no whole-unit rounding.
edge_cases.outcome: The third step is skipped.

edge_cases.case: The reader chooses thousands or millions.
edge_cases.outcome: The figure is divided by the scale and rendered with one decimal.

worked_examples.description: A figure of one million two hundred and thirty-four thousand five hundred and sixty-seven point eight nine, with whole-unit rounding and the thousands unit
