result.stored_or_displayed: Written as a carry-over external value dated the last day of the closed month, targeting the carry-in expression of the box for a previous period debt.

edge_cases.case: The debt is one hundred or more.
edge_cases.outcome: The clamp returns one hundred, because the clause clamps rather than zeroes; the law carries only a small debt and the rest is paid.

edge_cases.case: The month is in credit.
edge_cases.outcome: The payable line is zero, the clamp returns zero and nothing is carried on this side.

edge_cases.case: Two carry-overs run in parallel on this line.
edge_cases.outcome: The debt side and the credit side each have their own explicit target, because both carry-out expressions live on the result line while the two carry-in expressions live on two other lines.

worked_examples.description: A month with a payable of forty-five
worked_examples.narrative: Forty-five lies strictly between zero and one hundred, so the whole debt is carried and one external value of forty-five, dated the last day of the month, targets the carry-in expression of the box for a previous period debt.

worked_examples.description: A month with a payable of two thousand four hundred
worked_examples.narrative: Two thousand four hundred is at or above the upper bound, so the clamp returns one hundred rather than zero, which a rebuild must reproduce exactly.

records.name: The credit carried out of the Italian monthly return
records.purpose: Carries any credit of the month into the next month's box for a previous period credit, using the floor at zero and an explicit carry-over target.

operands.name: the tax credit of the month
operands.source: the credit column of the result line
operands.constraints: already floored at zero

operands.name: the bound of the clause
operands.source: the clause that keeps a value only above zero, written in euros
operands.constraints: zero

operands.name: the explicit carry-over target
operands.source: the carry-over target field of the expression
operands.constraints: names the carry-in expression of the box for a previous period credit

preconditions.condition: The carry-over target is stated explicitly.
preconditions.otherwise: The automatic resolution could not find it, because the carry-in expression lives on another line.

preconditions.condition: The period is actually closed.
preconditions.otherwise: The amount is computed and remembered but no record is written.

procedure: Read the tax credit of the month.
Keep it when it is strictly above zero, and return zero otherwise.
When the period is closed and the result is not zero, write one external value targeting the carry-in expression of the box for a previous period credit, dated the last day of the month.
records.formula: VP14._carryover_credit = VP14.credit    when VP14.credit > 0, else 0

rounding.precision: The decimal places of the presentation currency.
rounding.step: Once, at display; the operands are read unrounded.

result.name: the credit carried to the next month
result.stored_or_displayed: Written as a carry-over external value dated the last day of the closed month, targeting the carry-in expression of the box for a previous period credit.

edge_cases.case: The credit is large.
edge_cases.outcome: The whole credit is carried, because this side carries no upper bound, unlike the debt side.

edge_cases.case: The month is in debt.
edge_cases.outcome: The credit line is zero and nothing is carried on this side.

edge_cases.case: Re-closing the month.
edge_cases.outcome: The existing record is overwritten and the credit is never doubled.

worked_examples.description: A month in debt, on which nothing is carried on the credit side
worked_examples.narrative: Zero is not above zero, so nothing is carried and no record is written.

worked_examples.description: A month with a credit of one thousand two hundred and forty
worked_examples.narrative: One thousand two hundred and forty is above zero, so the whole credit is carried into the next month.

records.name: The use-in-tax-closing flag of a repartition line
records.purpose: Decides which tax lines a closing clears, which separates the tax the company must remit from the tax that is a cost or a revenue in its own books.

operands.name: the repartition type of the repartition line
operands.unit_or_currency: the value that stands for a share of the tax, or the value that stands for a share of the base
operands.source: the tax's repartition line
operands.constraints: only a share of the tax may be closed

operands.name: the account of the repartition line
operands.source: the tax's repartition line
operands.constraints: must be set

operands.name: the internal group of that account
operands.source: the account
operands.constraints: must be neither income nor expense

operands.name: the manual override
operands.source: the repartition line
operands.constraints: may be set by hand per repartition line

preconditions.condition: The repartition line belongs to a tax of the company being closed.
preconditions.otherwise: It is not considered at all.

preconditions.condition: The flag has not been overridden by hand.
preconditions.otherwise: The manual value is used instead of the computed one.

procedure: Answer yes when the repartition type is the one that stands for a share of the tax, an account is set on the repartition line, and that account's internal group is neither income nor expense.
Answer no otherwise.
Let a manual override on the repartition line replace the computed answer.
Keep, for the closing, only the tax lines of the period whose repartition line answers yes.
records.formula:
use_in_tax_closing = ( repartition type is the share of the tax )
                 AND ( an account is set on the repartition line )
                 AND ( the account's internal group is neither income nor expense )

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded: the answer is a yes or no value.
rounding.precision: Not applicable.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: the repartition line participates in the closing
result.stored_or_displayed: Not displayed; it selects the tax lines the closing entry clears, and it also decides whether the repartition line propagates the document's analytic distribution.

edge_cases.case: A non-deductible tax posted to an expense account.
edge_cases.outcome: The flag is false: the amount is a cost, not a tax to remit, and it is excluded from the closing.

edge_cases.case: A tax posted to a liability or asset account.
edge_cases.outcome: The flag is true and the amount is closed.

edge_cases.case: A repartition line whose flag is true.
edge_cases.outcome: It does not propagate the document's analytic distribution to its Journal Item, which is precisely why the closing entry carries none.

edge_cases.case: The flag is overridden by hand.
edge_cases.outcome: The manual value wins over the computed one.

worked_examples.description: Four tax accounts of a quarter
worked_examples.narrative: The three accounts whose internal group is neither income nor expense are kept; the account whose internal group is expense is excluded, because its tax is a cost.

records.name: The closing amount of a tax account
records.purpose: Totals, per tax account, the movement the period produced, which is the amount the closing entry reverses out of that account.

operands.name: the kept tax items on the account
operands.source: the tax lines of the period whose repartition line participates in the closing
operands.constraints: restricted by the base restriction with the only-tax-exigible flag on

operands.name: the debit and credit of each item
operands.source: the Journal Item
operands.constraints: not negative

preconditions.condition: The only-tax-exigible flag is applied.
preconditions.otherwise: A payment-basis tax whose cash has not moved would be closed before it is due.

preconditions.condition: The items are grouped by account.
preconditions.otherwise: The closing entry could not produce one line per account.

procedure: Take the tax lines of the period whose repartition line participates in the closing, on that account.
Add the debit and subtract the credit of each of them.
Round the total to the decimal places of the company currency.
Keep the tax group of each item's tax, for the counterpart step.
records.formula: account_closing_amount = Σ over the kept items m on that account of ( debit(m) − credit(m) )

rounding.precision: The decimal places of the company currency.
rounding.step: Once per account line, before the counterpart is derived as the balancing figure.

result.name: closing amount of the account
result.stored_or_displayed: Not displayed on the report; it becomes one line of the closing entry, on the side opposite to its sign.

edge_cases.case: The amount is negative.
edge_cases.outcome: The account carries a credit balance, which for a sales tax account means tax the company owes; the closing entry debits the account by the negated amount.

edge_cases.case: The amount is positive.
edge_cases.outcome: The account carries a debit balance, which for a purchase tax account means tax the company may reclaim; the closing entry credits the account by that amount.

edge_cases.case: The amount is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: No line is produced for that account.

edge_cases.case: The account had a balance from an earlier unclosed period.
edge_cases.outcome: Only the period's own movements are reversed, so the account is brought back to the balance it had at the start of the period and not to zero.

worked_examples.description: Three tax accounts of a quarter
worked_examples.narrative: The two accounts that collected tax total credits of eighteen thousand four hundred and twenty point three five and one thousand two hundred and four; the deductible account totals a debit of twelve thousand eight hundred and six point one five.

records.name: The net position of a tax closing
records.purpose: Adds the closing amounts of every kept account into the single figure that says whether the company owes the authorities or the authorities owe the company.

operands.name: the closing amounts of the kept accounts
operands.source: the amount per account
operands.constraints: one per account with a non-zero movement

preconditions.condition: Every kept account's amount has been computed over the same restriction.
preconditions.otherwise: The net position does not tie to the accounts.

procedure: Add the closing amounts of every kept account.
Read a negative result as a balance in favour of the authorities: the company owes the negated amount.
Read a positive result as a balance in favour of the company: the authorities owe that amount.
Read a zero result as a position where the individual accounts still zero against each other and no counterpart line is produced.
records.formula:
net_position = Σ over all the kept accounts of account_closing_amount
amount_owed  = − net_position    when net_position < 0

rounding.precision: The decimal places of the company currency.
rounding.step: Once per account line, before the counterpart is derived as the balancing figure.

result.name: net position of the closing
result.stored_or_displayed: Not displayed on the report; it decides the counterpart line of the closing entry and whether an advance payment may be consumed.

edge_cases.case: The net position is negative.
edge_cases.outcome: The company owes the negated amount and the counterpart is a credit on the tax payable account.

edge_cases.case: The net position is positive.
edge_cases.outcome: The authorities owe that amount and the counterpart is a debit on the tax receivable account.

edge_cases.case: The net position is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The closing entry still zeroes the individual accounts against each other and produces no counterpart line.

edge_cases.case: Several tax groups are involved.
edge_cases.outcome: Each group has its own net position and its own counterpart, so the two amounts can be paid to different authorities on different dates.

worked_examples.description: A quarter in favour of the authorities
worked_examples.narrative: Minus eighteen thousand four hundred and twenty point three five, minus one thousand two hundred and four, plus twelve thousand eight hundred and six point one five is minus six thousand eight hundred and eighteen point two zero, so the company owes six thousand eight hundred and eighteen point two zero.

worked_examples.description: A quarter in favour of the company
worked_examples.narrative: Minus four thousand one hundred plus nine thousand three hundred and fifty is five thousand two hundred and fifty, which the authorities owe.

records.name: The balance of an advance tax payment account
records.purpose: Reads what a company has already paid on account to the authorities, which is the amount a closing may consume before asking for the rest.

operands.name: the items on the advance account of the tax group
operands.source: the ledger up to the closing date
operands.constraints: the closing date is the last day of the period being closed

operands.name: the debit and credit of each item
operands.source: the Journal Item
operands.constraints: not negative

preconditions.condition: The tax group carries an advance tax payment account.
preconditions.otherwise: No advance is consumed and the whole amount owed goes to the counterpart line.

preconditions.condition: The balance of that account is not zero at the closing date.
preconditions.otherwise: No advance line is produced.

procedure: Take the Journal Items on the advance tax payment account of the tax group whose accounting date is on or before the closing date.
Add the debit and subtract the credit of each of them.
Use the result only when the net position of the group is in favour of the authorities.
records.formula:
advance_balance = Σ over the items on the advance account of the group,
                    with accounting date ≤ closing_entry_date,
                    of ( debit − credit )

rounding.precision: The decimal places of the company currency.
rounding.step: Once per account line, before the counterpart is derived as the balancing figure.

result.name: balance of the advance account
result.stored_or_displayed: Not displayed on the report; it bounds the amount the closing entry credits to the advance account.

edge_cases.case: The net position is in favour of the company.
edge_cases.outcome: No advance is consumed at all, because the rule applies only when the company owes.

edge_cases.case: The advance account is reconcilable.
edge_cases.outcome: The advance line of the closing entry is reconciled against the advance payments it consumes, oldest first.

edge_cases.case: Payments were made after the closing date.
edge_cases.outcome: They are excluded, because only items up to the closing date are read.

worked_examples.description: An advance account carrying one instalment paid inside the quarter
worked_examples.narrative: The instalment of two thousand was paid before the closing date, so the advance balance is two thousand.

records.name: The advance payment consumed by a closing
records.purpose: Consumes as much of the advance already paid as the debt allows, leaving any excess on the advance account for the next period.

operands.name: the advance balance
operands.source: the advance tax payment account of the tax group at the closing date
operands.constraints: positive when an instalment was paid

operands.name: the amount owed
operands.source: the negated net position of the group
operands.constraints: the rule applies only when the net position is below zero

preconditions.condition: The net position of the group is in favour of the authorities.
preconditions.otherwise: No advance is consumed: the offset is zero.

preconditions.condition: The advance balance is positive.
preconditions.otherwise: There is nothing to consume.

procedure: Check that the net position is below zero, that is that the company owes.
Take the smaller of the advance balance and the amount owed.
Credit the advance tax payment account by that amount, which consumes the instalment already paid.
Leave any excess on the advance account for the next period.
records.formula:
amount_offset = min( advance_balance , − net_position )    when net_position < 0
amount_offset = 0                                          otherwise

rounding.precision: The decimal places of the company currency.
rounding.step: Once per account line, before the counterpart is derived as the balancing figure.

result.name: advance payment consumed
result.stored_or_displayed: Not displayed on the report; it becomes the advance line of the closing entry, always a credit.

edge_cases.case: The advance balance exceeds the amount owed.
edge_cases.outcome: Only the amount owed is consumed and the excess stays on the advance account for the next period.

edge_cases.case: The amount owed exceeds the advance balance.
edge_cases.outcome: The whole advance is consumed and the rest goes to the counterpart line.

edge_cases.case: The net position is in favour of the company.
edge_cases.outcome: Nothing is consumed, because the rule applies only when the company owes.

worked_examples.description: An advance of two thousand against a debt of six thousand eight hundred and eighteen point two zero
worked_examples.narrative: Two thousand is the smaller of the two, so the whole advance is consumed and the account is brought to zero.

worked_examples.description: An advance of nine thousand against the same debt
worked_examples.narrative: Six thousand eight hundred and eighteen point two zero is the smaller of the two, so only that much is consumed and two thousand one hundred and eighty-one point eight zero stays on the advance account.

records.name: The amount remaining after the advance payment
records.purpose: Gives the part of the debt the advance did not cover, which is what the counterpart line of the closing entry puts on the tax payable account.

operands.name: the amount owed
operands.source: the negated net position of the group
operands.constraints: positive when the company owes

operands.name: the advance payment consumed
operands.source: the offset calculation
operands.constraints: never more than the amount owed

preconditions.condition: The net position is in favour of the authorities.
preconditions.otherwise: There is no remainder: the counterpart is a debit on the tax receivable account for the whole net position.

preconditions.condition: The tax group has a tax payable account.
preconditions.otherwise: The validation is refused, because the counterpart has no account to go to.

procedure: Take the amount owed, that is the negated net position.
Subtract the advance payment consumed.
Credit the tax payable account of the group by the remainder when it is above zero, and produce no payable line when it is zero.
records.formula: remaining = ( − net_position ) − amount_offset

rounding.precision: The decimal places of the company currency.
rounding.step: Once per account line, before the counterpart is derived as the balancing figure.

result.name: amount remaining to pay
result.stored_or_displayed: Not displayed on the report; it becomes the counterpart line of the closing entry on the tax payable account, which the subsequent payment is reconciled against.

edge_cases.case: The advance covered the whole debt.
edge_cases.outcome: The remainder is zero and no payable line is produced.

edge_cases.case: There is no advance account.
edge_cases.outcome: The remainder equals the amount owed.

edge_cases.case: The net position is in favour of the company.
edge_cases.outcome: This calculation does not apply: the counterpart is a debit on the tax receivable account for the whole net position.

worked_examples.description: A debt of six thousand eight hundred and eighteen point two zero against an advance of two thousand
worked_examples.narrative: Six thousand eight hundred and eighteen point two zero less two thousand is four thousand eight hundred and eighteen point two zero, which the company still owes.

worked_examples.description: The same debt against an advance of nine thousand
worked_examples.narrative: The advance covered the whole debt, so no payable line is produced.

records.name: The rounding of the closing lines and the counterpart as the balancing figure
records.purpose: Rounds each account line first and derives the counterpart as the balancing figure of the already-rounded lines, so that the closing entry balances to the cent by construction.

operands.name: the closing amount of each account
operands.source: the amount per account
operands.constraints: rounded before the counterpart is derived

operands.name: the advance line
operands.source: the advance payment consumed
operands.constraints: already rounded

operands.name: the sign convention of each line
operands.source: the sign of the account's amount
operands.constraints: a negative amount becomes a debit of its negation and a positive amount becomes a credit of itself

preconditions.condition: Every account line is rounded before the counterpart is computed.
preconditions.otherwise: Rounding the net position independently could leave an imbalance of one hundredth of the currency unit.

preconditions.condition: The counterpart is derived from the rounded lines.
preconditions.otherwise: The entry may not balance.

procedure: Round each account's closing amount to the decimal places of the company currency.
Place each rounded amount on the opposite side to its sign: a negative amount becomes a debit of its negation, a positive amount becomes a credit of itself, and a zero amount produces no line.
Place the advance payment consumed as a credit on the advance account, when there is one.
Compute the counterpart as the negated sum of the signed amounts of the account lines and the advance line.

Partition the account lines by tax group first when several groups are involved, so that each group's counterpart is its own balancing figure and the sum of the counterparts equals the overall balancing figure.
records.formula:
counterpart_amount = − Σ over the account lines and the advance line of rounded_amount
                   = − Σ over those lines of ( debit − credit )

rounding.what: Each account line, before the counterpart is derived.
rounding.precision: The decimal places of the company currency.
rounding.step: On each line, before the counterpart; never on the net position independently.

result.name: counterpart amount
result.stored_or_displayed: Placed on the tax payable account as a credit when it is negative, and on the tax receivable account as a debit when it is positive; the closing entry then balances exactly.

edge_cases.case: Several tax groups are involved.
edge_cases.outcome: Each group's account lines are partitioned first and each group's counterpart is its own balancing figure, so every group balances on its own.

edge_cases.case: The net position is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: No counterpart line is produced and the account lines still zero against each other.

edge_cases.case: The counterpart is rounded independently.
edge_cases.outcome: A one-cent imbalance can appear, which is exactly what this ordering prevents.

edge_cases.case: The counterpart account is reconcilable.
edge_cases.outcome: The counterpart line is reconciled against the subsequent payment or refund.

worked_examples.description: A quarter with three account lines and no advance
worked_examples.narrative: The signed sum of the three rounded lines is six thousand eight hundred and eighteen point two zero, so the counterpart is minus that figure, a credit of six thousand eight hundred and eighteen point two zero, and the entry totals nineteen thousand six hundred and twenty-four point three five on each side.

worked_examples.description: The same quarter with an advance line of two thousand
worked_examples.narrative: The account lines and the advance line together give four thousand eight hundred and eighteen point two zero, so the counterpart is a credit of that amount and the entry still balances at nineteen thousand six hundred and twenty-four point three five on each side.

records.name: The accounting date of the closing entry
records.purpose: Dates the closing entry on the period it closes rather than on the day the user acted, so that a return validated late still closes its own period. The ledger effects are itemised in the accounting effects document of this folder, to which this section points.

operands.name: the period being closed
operands.unit_or_currency: a first day and a last day
operands.source: the tax return being validated
operands.constraints: one company, one tax report and one period

operands.name: the day the user validated
operands.source: the action
operands.constraints: deliberately not used as the accounting date

preconditions.condition: A tax return is moving from the state that means it is under review to the state that means it has been reviewed.
preconditions.otherwise: No closing entry is produced at all.

preconditions.condition: The company has a tax return journal.
preconditions.otherwise: The validation is refused, because the entry has no journal to be posted in.

procedure: Take the last day of the period being closed.
Use it as the accounting date of the closing entry, whatever the day the user pressed the validation.
Post the entry in the company's tax return journal, which is a journal of the miscellaneous type configured on the company, and number it from that journal's sequence.
records.formula: closing_entry_date = last day of the period being closed

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded: the result is a date.
rounding.precision: Whole days.
rounding.step: No rounding step.

result.name: accounting date of the closing entry
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the Journal Entry; it also fixes the date the tax return lock date moves to and the date the carry-over external values carry.

edge_cases.case: A monthly return closing March.
edge_cases.outcome: The date is the thirty-first of March.

edge_cases.case: A quarterly return closing the second quarter of a calendar fiscal year.
edge_cases.outcome: The date is the thirtieth of June.

edge_cases.case: The return is validated weeks later.
edge_cases.outcome: The date is unchanged: it is the period's last day, not the day of the action.

edge_cases.case: The tax return journal runs in restricted mode.
edge_cases.outcome: The entry joins the hash chain and can no longer be reset to draft; it may only be reversed.

worked_examples.description: A quarterly return validated in July for the second quarter
worked_examples.narrative: The date is the last day of the closed period and not the day of the validation.

records.name: The side and the amount of a tax account line of the closing entry
records.purpose: Turns each account's closing amount into one line of the closing entry, on the side that reverses the period's movement. The line itself is specified in the accounting effects document of this folder, which this section points to.

operands.name: the closing amount of the account
operands.source: the amount per account, already rounded
operands.constraints: may be negative, positive or zero

operands.name: the account
operands.source: the tax lines kept for the closing
operands.constraints: one line per account

preconditions.condition: The closing amount is not zero.
preconditions.otherwise: No line is produced for that account.

preconditions.condition: The account was selected by the rules that say which amounts are closed.
preconditions.otherwise: It has no place in the entry.

procedure: Read the closing amount of the account, rounded to the company currency.
When the amount is negative, that is when the account carries a credit balance, place a debit of the negated amount on that account.
When the amount is positive, that is when the account carries a debit balance, place a credit of that amount on that account.
Produce no line when the amount is zero.
Give every line the company currency, no partner, no analytic distribution, no tax, no tax line reference and no tag.
records.formula:
line_side   = debit  and line_amount = − account_amount( a )    when account_amount( a ) < 0
line_side   = credit and line_amount =   account_amount( a )    when account_amount( a ) > 0
no line is produced                                              when account_amount( a ) = 0

rounding.precision: The decimal places of the company currency.
rounding.step: Once per line, before the counterpart is derived as the balancing figure.

result.name: the account lines of the closing entry
result.stored_or_displayed: Posted as Journal Items of the closing entry; the tax accounts are brought back to the balance they had at the start of the period, not to zero.

edge_cases.case: An output tax account.
edge_cases.outcome: It carries a credit balance, so the line is a debit that clears the period's collection.

edge_cases.case: An input tax account.
edge_cases.outcome: It carries a debit balance, so the line is a credit that clears the period's deduction.

edge_cases.case: The account had a balance from an earlier unclosed period.
edge_cases.outcome: It is untouched: only the period's own movements are reversed, and a rebuild that zeroed the account outright would destroy the earlier period's balance.

edge_cases.case: The line carries a foreign currency in the underlying tax lines.
edge_cases.outcome: The closing line is still in the company currency only; foreign currency exposure is handled by the exchange-difference mechanism of the multi-currency documents.

worked_examples.description: Three tax accounts of a quarter
worked_examples.narrative: The two credit balances become debits of eighteen thousand four hundred and twenty point three five and one thousand two hundred and four; the debit balance becomes a credit of twelve thousand eight hundred and six point one five.

records.name: The side and the amount of the counterpart line of the closing entry
records.purpose: Places the position of the closing on the payable or the receivable account of the tax group, which is the open item the payment or the refund will be reconciled against. The line is specified in the accounting effects document of this folder.

operands.name: the amount remaining after the advance
operands.source: the remainder calculation
operands.constraints: positive when the company still owes

operands.name: the net position of the group
operands.source: the net position calculation
operands.constraints: positive when the authorities owe

operands.name: the tax payable account of the group
operands.source: the tax group
operands.constraints: required when the company owes

operands.name: the tax receivable account of the group
operands.source: the tax group
operands.constraints: required when the authorities owe

preconditions.condition: The tax group has a payable account when the company owes, and a receivable account when it is owed.
preconditions.otherwise: The validation is refused.

preconditions.condition: The counterpart is derived as the balancing figure of the already-rounded lines.
preconditions.otherwise: A one-cent imbalance can appear.

procedure: When the remainder is above zero, credit the tax payable account of the group by the remainder.
When the net position is above zero, debit the tax receivable account of the group by the net position.
Produce no counterpart line when the net position is zero and no advance is consumed.
Give the line no partner: the authority is not modelled as a partner on the closing entry.
Reconcile the line against the subsequent payment or refund when the account is flagged reconcilable.
records.formula:
counterpart = credit of remaining( g ) on the tax payable account    when remaining( g ) > 0
counterpart = debit  of net_position( g ) on the tax receivable account when net_position( g ) > 0
no counterpart line                                                     when net_position( g ) = 0 and no advance is consumed

rounding.precision: The decimal places of the company currency.
rounding.step: Once per line, before the counterpart is derived as the balancing figure.

result.name: the counterpart line of the closing entry
result.stored_or_displayed: Posted as a Journal Item on the tax payable or the tax receivable account; it is the open item the payment or the refund settles.

edge_cases.case: An advance covered the whole debt.
edge_cases.outcome: The remainder is zero and no payable line is produced; the advance line alone balances the entry.

edge_cases.case: The authorities owe the company.
edge_cases.outcome: The counterpart is a debit on the receivable account for the whole net position, and no advance is consumed.

edge_cases.case: Several tax groups are involved.
edge_cases.outcome: One counterpart per group, each balancing its own group, which is what lets the amounts be paid to different authorities on different dates.

edge_cases.case: The counterpart account is not configured.
edge_cases.outcome: The validation is refused by the precondition that requires the tax payable and receivable accounts.

worked_examples.description: A quarter in favour of the authorities with an advance of two thousand
worked_examples.narrative: The advance account is credited by two thousand and the payable account by the remaining four thousand eight hundred and eighteen point two zero.

worked_examples.description: A quarter in favour of the company
worked_examples.narrative: The receivable account is debited by five thousand two hundred and fifty, which is what the authorities owe.

records.name: The per-company closing entries of a tax unit
records.purpose: Splits one consolidated declaration into one closing entry per company, because a Journal Entry may never span companies, and moves the members' positions to the representative through intercompany accounts.

operands.name: the companies of the tax unit
operands.source: the tax unit
operands.constraints: one entry per company

operands.name: the amounts of each company
operands.unit_or_currency: the company currency of that company
operands.source: that company's own tax accounts
operands.constraints: only that company's amounts enter its entry

operands.name: the net position of each member
operands.source: the member's own closing
operands.constraints: moved to the representative

operands.name: the intercompany accounts
operands.source: the company settings for intercompany balances
operands.constraints: when they are not configured, the unit closing is refused

preconditions.condition: The intercompany accounts are configured.
preconditions.otherwise: The unit closing is refused.

preconditions.condition: The returns of the unit are validated together.
preconditions.otherwise: The representative's entry cannot carry the members' positions.

procedure: Render the report for the whole unit, so that every engine reads the Journal Items of every company of the unit and the figures are the consolidated ones.
Produce one closing entry per company, each clearing only that company's tax accounts and each balancing on its own.

On the representative's entry, add one line per other company: when a member owes an amount, credit the tax payable account by that amount and debit the intercompany receivable account of that member by the same amount; when a member is owed an amount, debit the tax receivable account and credit the intercompany payable account.

On the member's entry, replace its own counterpart line by a credit of the intercompany payable account of the representative when it owes, and by a debit of the intercompany receivable account of the representative when it is owed.
Move every company's tax return lock date to the last day of the closed period.
records.formula:
one closing entry per company of the unit, each balancing on its own
representative_entry = its own closing lines + one intercompany pair per member
member_position moved to the representative through the intercompany accounts

rounding.precision: The decimal places of the company currency.
rounding.step: Once per line, before the counterpart is derived as the balancing figure.

result.name: the closing entries of the unit
result.unit_or_currency: the company currency of each company
result.stored_or_displayed: Posted one per company; the representative holds the whole amount to pay towards the authorities.

edge_cases.case: A member owes an amount.
edge_cases.outcome: The representative credits the tax payable account and debits the intercompany receivable account of that member, while the member credits the intercompany payable account of the representative.

edge_cases.case: A member is owed an amount.
edge_cases.outcome: The representative debits the tax receivable account and credits the intercompany payable account, while the member debits the intercompany receivable account of the representative.

edge_cases.case: The intercompany accounts are missing.
edge_cases.outcome: The unit closing is refused.

edge_cases.case: A tax unit is selected while the report's multi-company switch works by selector.
edge_cases.outcome: The unit is ignored and the companies are treated individually.

worked_examples.description: A unit of two companies where the member owes one thousand four hundred and sixty
worked_examples.narrative: The member moves its one thousand four hundred and sixty to the representative through the intercompany pair, and the representative's payable line carries its own six thousand eight hundred and eighteen point two zero plus that amount, that is eight thousand two hundred and seventy-eight point two zero.

records.name: The new tax return lock date after a validation
records.purpose: Moves the company's tax return lock date to the end of the closed period and never backwards, which is what records that a period has been declared. The side effect is specified in the accounting effects document of this folder.

operands.name: the current tax return lock date of the company
operands.source: the company
operands.constraints: may already be later than the closed period

operands.name: the last day of the closed period
operands.source: the period being closed
operands.constraints: the candidate new value

preconditions.condition: A tax return is being validated.
preconditions.otherwise: The lock date is unchanged.

preconditions.condition: The candidate date is later than the current one.
preconditions.otherwise: The lock date is unchanged, because it only ever moves forward at a validation.

procedure: Take the current tax return lock date of the company, treating an absent value as earlier than any date.
Take the last day of the closed period.
Set the lock date to the later of the two.
Write the change to the company's tracked message log, so that the date the period was closed is itself auditable.
records.formula: new_tax_lock_date = max( current_tax_lock_date , last day of the closed period )

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded: the result is a date.
rounding.precision: Whole days.
rounding.step: No rounding step.

result.name: tax return lock date
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the company and tracked in its message log; it governs which entries carrying taxes may still be written.

edge_cases.case: A new entry carrying taxes is dated on or before the lock date.
edge_cases.outcome: Its accounting date is postponed to the first date after the lock date that its journal's sequence allows; the entry is not refused.

edge_cases.case: An existing posted entry carrying taxes is dated on or before the lock date.
edge_cases.outcome: It cannot be modified or reset.

edge_cases.case: A lock date exception exists.
edge_cases.outcome: The restriction is lifted for a named user for a bounded time, because this is a soft lock date.

edge_cases.case: The validation is cancelled or the return is reset to draft.
edge_cases.outcome: The lock date is not moved back; moving it back is an explicit act requiring the group that may change lock dates.

edge_cases.case: The hard lock date.
edge_cases.outcome: It admits no exception at all and is never moved by this domain.

worked_examples.description: A company whose lock date is the thirty-first of March closing the second quarter
worked_examples.narrative: The later of the two dates is the thirtieth of June, so the lock date moves forward.

worked_examples.description: The same company re-closing the first quarter afterwards
worked_examples.narrative: The current date is already later, so the lock date does not move back.

records.name: The hash of a secured entry
records.purpose: Chains each entry of a journal running in restricted mode to the one before it, so that a change to any hashed value of any entry breaks the chain and can be detected.

operands.name: the entry's own hashed fields
operands.source: the Journal Entry: its number, its accounting date, its journal and its company for the current hash version, which is the fourth
operands.constraints: the journal and the company are rendered as their stored numeric identifiers, the date in its canonical text form; for the first hash version the number is not part of the input

operands.name: the hashed fields of each item
operands.source: the Journal Items, in the order they are stored: the label, the debit, the credit, the account and the partner for the current version
operands.constraints: for the first hash version the label is not included; from the third version onwards monetary fields are rendered with exactly the currency's decimal places

operands.name: the previous hash
operands.source: the hash of the previous entry of the chain
operands.constraints: only the digest part after the second dollar sign is used

operands.name: the hash version
operands.unit_or_currency: a whole number from one to four
operands.source: the entry
operands.constraints: the current version is the fourth

preconditions.condition: The journal runs in restricted mode.
preconditions.otherwise: The entry is not hashed at all.

preconditions.condition: The numbering of the entries to hash has no gap inside the range being chained.
preconditions.otherwise: The hashing stops with the message that an error occurred when computing the inalterability and that a gap has been detected in the sequence.

procedure: Build a mapping of the entry's own hashed fields to text, rendering the journal and the company as their stored numeric identifiers and the date in its canonical text form.

For each item of the entry, in the order the items are stored, add one entry to the mapping per hashed item field, keyed by the fixed prefix for a line, the item's numeric identifier, an underscore and the field name.
Render monetary fields with exactly the decimal places of the currency, so that trailing zeroes cannot change the hash.

Serialize the mapping to a textual object notation with the keys sorted, with only characters of the basic character set, with no indentation, with a comma between pairs and a colon between a key and its value.

Concatenate the previous hash digest and that text, in that order, and take the digest of the concatenation with the secure hash algorithm of two hundred and fifty-six bits, rendered in lowercase hexadecimal.
Prefix the digest with a dollar sign, the hash version number and another dollar sign.
records.formula:
hash_input  = previous_hash_digest + serialized_fields
hash_digest = secure_hash_256( hash_input )
stored_hash = "$" + version + "$" + hash_digest

rounding.what: Monetary fields, before they enter the serialized text.
rounding.precision: Exactly the decimal places of the currency, from the third hash version onwards.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, as everywhere in the ledger.
rounding.step: While the mapping is built, so that trailing zeroes cannot change the digest.

result.name: stored hash of the entry
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the Journal Entry and used as the previous hash of the next entry of the chain.

edge_cases.case: The previous hash carries a version prefix.
edge_cases.outcome: Only the digest part after the second dollar sign is used; the version prefix never enters the computation.

edge_cases.case: The entry is the first of its chain.
edge_cases.outcome: There is no previous hash and the concatenation starts with an empty text.

edge_cases.case: A hashed field is edited afterwards.
edge_cases.outcome: The recomputed hash no longer matches the stored one and the entry is reported as corrupted; the locking rules forbid the edit in the first place.

edge_cases.case: An item is added or removed.
edge_cases.outcome: The mapping changes and the hash changes with it, which is why the item fields are part of the input.

worked_examples.description: An entry of the fourth hash version with two items

expected_outputs.stored_hash_shape: a dollar sign, the version four, a dollar sign and sixty-four lowercase hexadecimal characters

worked_examples.narrative: Four entry fields plus five fields for each of the two items give fourteen mapping entries, which are serialized with sorted keys, concatenated behind the previous digest and hashed into sixty-four hexadecimal characters carrying the version prefix.

records.name: The verification of the hash chain of a journal
records.purpose: Recomputes every stored hash of every journal in order and reports, per journal and per numbering prefix, whether the chain is intact, so that an auditor can rely on the ledger being unaltered.

operands.name: the journals of the company
operands.source: the company
operands.constraints: each is noted as running in restricted mode or not

operands.name: the hashed entries of a journal
operands.source: the journal
operands.constraints: ordered by the secured sequence number ascending with entries having none last, then by the sequence prefix, then by the sequence number ascending

operands.name: the stored hash of each entry
operands.source: the Journal Entry
operands.constraints: carries its version as a prefix

operands.name: the maximum hash version
operands.source: the hashing rules
operands.constraints: four

preconditions.condition: The requesting user holds the accounting user group.
preconditions.otherwise: The check is refused with the message "Please contact your accountant to print the Hash integrity result."

preconditions.condition: The journal has at least one hashed entry.
preconditions.otherwise: The finding is that there is no journal entry flagged for accounting data inalterability yet.

procedure: Note, for each journal, whether it runs in restricted mode.
Select every entry of that journal carrying a hash, ordered by the secured sequence number ascending with entries having none last, then by the sequence prefix, then by the sequence number ascending.

Walk the selected entries in batches of one thousand, clearing the read cache between batches so that a very long chain can be verified without holding the whole ledger in memory, and maintain per sequence prefix the first verified entry, the last verified entry and the first corrupted entry, and also the last verified entry across all prefixes.

For each entry, take as the previous hash the hash of the last verified entry of the same prefix, unless the entry carries a secured sequence number, in which case take the hash of the last verified entry overall.
Recompute the hash from version one upwards until it matches the stored hash or the maximum version, four, is exceeded.
Record the entry as the corrupted entry of its prefix and skip the rest of that prefix when no version matches, and record it as the prefix's last verified entry otherwise.

Read the entries with full privileges regardless of the requesting user's record-level access, because a partial read would produce a different hash, and use only the digest, never the values themselves.
records.formula:
for each entry e of a prefix, in order:
    previous = hash( last verified entry of the same prefix )
    previous = hash( last verified entry overall )    when e carries a secured sequence number
    verified( e ) = there exists a version v in 1 … 4 with recompute( e , v , previous ) = stored_hash( e )

rounding.precision: Exactly the decimal places of the currency, from the third hash version onwards.
rounding.step: Inside the hash computation, never on the findings.

result.name: one finding per journal and prefix
result.unit_or_currency: a status, a message and the bounding entries
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed in the integrity result: the status, the journal's name followed by its sequence prefix in parentheses, a flag reading the letter that stands for a journal in restricted mode or the letter that stands for one that is not, and, for a verified prefix, the first and the last entry's number, hash and date.

edge_cases.case: The journal has no hashed entry at all.
edge_cases.outcome: The finding is that there is no journal entry flagged for accounting data inalterability yet.

edge_cases.case: An entry's stored hash matches no version.
edge_cases.outcome: The finding names it as corrupted data on the journal entry with its identifier and its entry number, and every later entry of that prefix is skipped, so only the first corruption is named.

edge_cases.case: Every entry of a prefix recomputes correctly.
edge_cases.outcome: The finding says the entries are correctly hashed and carries the first and the last entry's number, hash and date.

edge_cases.case: The requesting user's record-level access hides some entries.
edge_cases.outcome: They are read anyway with full privileges, because a partial read would produce a different hash; only the digest is used.

edge_cases.case: The user does not hold the accounting user group.
edge_cases.outcome: The check is refused with the message that asks the user to contact their accountant to print the result.

worked_examples.description: A journal in restricted mode with one prefix of one thousand two hundred hashed entries, all intact
worked_examples.narrative: The entries are read in two batches of at most one thousand, every hash recomputes, and the finding says the entries are correctly hashed and carries the bounding entries.

worked_examples.description: The same journal with the four hundredth entry altered
worked_examples.narrative: The four hundredth entry matches no version from one to four, so it is recorded as the prefix's corruption and the remaining eight hundred entries of the prefix are skipped.
